title: Final fix: vectorSearch() auto-connects internally to preserve keepConnection=False lifecycle
content:
The definitive fix for the vector search lifecycle bug (isVectorSearchSupported() returning False on unconnected providers) was implemented in `SQLite3Provider.vectorSearch()` in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py`.

**Previous intermediate fix** (Option B, now superseded): A manual `await sqlProvider.connect()` was added in `_semanticSearch()` before the `isVectorSearchSupported()` check. This broke the `keepConnection=False` lifecycle — the SQLite3Provider cursor tracking sees `wasConnected=True` when connect() was called externally, so `cursor()` skips auto-disconnect, effectively pinning the provider open permanently.

**Final fix**: `vectorSearch()` now auto-connects internally before the capability check:
```python
if not self._vectorSearchAvailable and _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE:
    await self.connect()
```
The sqlite-vec extension is loaded inside `connect()`, so `_vectorSearchAvailable` stays `False` until a connection is established. The auto-connect fires once to detect capability and populate the flag; subsequent calls skip it since `_vectorSearchAvailable` is now `True`. The manual `connect()` was removed from `_semanticSearch()` — both the native path (through `vectorSearch()`) and the numpy path (through `executeFetchAll` → `cursor()` → `connect()`) self-connect. The `keepConnection=False` contract is restored: connections open and close per operation as intended.

**Files changed**: `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` and `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py`.

**Regression test added**: `test_vectorSearchAutoConnectsWhenUnconnected` in `tests/database/providers/test_sqlite3_vector_search.py` — verifies that calling `vectorSearch()` on a fresh unconnected provider succeeds (results returned + `_vectorSearchAvailable` flips to True) without the caller calling `connect()`. Without the fix this raises `NotImplementedError`.

title: Fix: _nativeVectorSearch maxMessages cutoff must JOIN message_embeddings filtered by model
content:
The `_nativeVectorSearch()` method in `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` computes a `minDate` cutoff when `maxMessages` is set, to limit how far back to search. The original cutoff query was:

```sql
SELECT date FROM chat_messages
WHERE chat_id = :chatId
ORDER BY date DESC
```

This counted ALL chat messages — including those without embeddings for the active model. During partial backfill or after a model change, recent chat messages lacking embeddings would shrink the native candidate pool differently than the numpy path, which filters via `message_embeddings JOIN chat_messages` filtered by `me.model = :modelName`.

**Fix**: The cutoff now JOINs `message_embeddings` and filters by model:

```sql
SELECT c.date
FROM message_embeddings me
JOIN chat_messages c
    ON c.chat_id = me.chat_id AND c.message_id = me.message_id
WHERE me.chat_id = :chatId AND me.model = :modelName
ORDER BY c.date DESC, me.message_id DESC
```

The `executeFetchOne` call now also passes `modelName` in params: `{"chatId": chatId, "modelName": modelName}`.

This ensures the native and numpy candidate pools are derived from the same row set, preventing divergence during partial backfill or after model changes.

**Files changed**: `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py`.

**Tests strengthened**: `test_nativeSearchWithMaxMessages` in `tests/database/repositories/test_chat_search_native.py` now asserts the cutoff query passed to `executeFetchOne` uses the `message_embeddings JOIN chat_messages` shape and that `modelName` is included in params.

title: Correction: test mock monkey-patching uses `# type: ignore[method-assign]` not `cast(Any, ...)`
content:
The "No Any type" hard rule in AGENTS.md applies to test code too. The previously recorded convention (memory 678cd785) recommending `cast(Any, handler)` for mock monkey-patching in tests is superseded.

The correct pattern is direct attribute assignment with a per-line pyright suppression:

```python
# Instead of:
handler = cast(Any, ChatSearchHandler(...))
handler.getChatSettings = AsyncMock(return_value=cs)

# Use:
handler = ChatSearchHandler(...)
handler.getChatSettings = AsyncMock(return_value=cs)  # type: ignore[method-assign]
```

This preserves concrete typing while silencing only the single line. The `[method-assign]` error code is preferred over a bare `# type: ignore` because it's more specific.

Files updated to this pattern: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py`. Removed `from typing import Any` and `cast(...)` imports entirely.

See also AGENTS.md §Hard rules: "No `Any` type. Never use `Any` except when a method genuinely accepts any type."

title: Critical integration gap: vec0 fast path activates on partial corpus, ignoring older authoritative embeddings
content:
GATE 2 REVIEW FINDING: The native search fast path in `_semanticSearch()` returns vec0 results whenever `_nativeVectorSearch()` returns any non-empty rows. After rollout, a chat with pre-existing `message_embeddings` (never backfilled into vec0) plus a few newly dual-written rows will search only that vec0 subset. Older messages become invisible as soon as vec0 returns any results.

This is distinct from the "empty vec0" fallback (already tracked in separate memory). The `if nativeResults:` guard handles the all-or-nothing case (empty vec0 → fall through to numpy), but NOT the partial case where vec0 has some rows. Even one vec0 row activates native-only search, ignoring all legacy authoritative embeddings.

FIXES:
1. Block native path until vec0 coverage is complete (e.g., count check between `message_embeddings` and `vec_message_embeddings_N`)
2. Backfill vec0 from `message_embeddings` before enabling the fast path
3. Or add a completeness guard that checks `isVectorSearchSupported()` AND confirms the vec0 table is fully populated

See `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` – `_nativeVectorSearch()` caller. No out-of-band migration or backfill step exists in the current diff. Without one, this is a release blocker.

title: vec0 native search applies post-filters after top-K — diverges from numpy pre-filter semantics
content:
GATE 2 REVIEW FINDING: The vec0 native search path (`_nativeVectorSearch`) fetches the global top-K nearest neighbors via `vectorSearch(k=topK, filterClause=...)`, then applies remaining filters (`userFilter`, `categoryFilter`, `rootMessageId`) on the already-ranked results. The numpy path loads all matching embeddings (pre-filtered by filter criteria), then ranks them all by cosine similarity. These are NOT equivalent.

IMPACT: Filtered semantic queries can miss valid hits or return < limit results whenever matching rows fall outside the unfiltered top-K. For example: a user filter matching only 3 messages, all ranked at positions 150-200 globally — these never enter the native top-K (assuming topK=50) and are silently dropped.

TEMPORARY WORKAROUND: Bypass native search when non-pushdown filters are present. At minimum, `maxAgeDays` CAN be pushed into `filterClause` since vec0 stores `date` as TEXT — this should be done.

FILE: `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` — `_semanticSearch()` native path vs numpy path.

title: maxMessages cutoff on timestamp ties: vec0 native path broader than numpy path
content:
GATE 2 REVIEW FINDING: When `maxMessages` limits the candidate pool, the authoritative numpy path selects the cutoff row with `ORDER BY c.date DESC, me.message_id DESC`, while the vec0 predicate only applies `date >= :minDate`. Messages sharing the cutoff timestamp but outside the authoritative top-N still enter the native candidate pool, so native and numpy can disagree even with a fully mirrored corpus.

IMPACT: Semantic search results can differ between native and numpy paths for chats where multiple messages share the same timestamp (common with Telegram's second-granularity dates). The discrepancy is bounded (only affects the date boundary) but causes non-deterministic result mismatches.

FIX: Carry both boundary fields (`minDate` and `minMessageId`) and filter with `(date > :minDate) OR (date = :minDate AND message_id >= :minMessageId)` instead of just `date >= :minDate`.

FILE: `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` — `_semanticSearch()` maxMessages logic for vec0 vs numpy paths.

title: Missing test coverage: partial vec0 corpus, selective post-filters, timestamp-boundary ties
content:
GATE 2 REVIEW FINDING: The current test suite (5 interface tests + 16 sqlite3 tests + 7 repository integration tests + 9 cleanup tests) covers helper behavior and provider mechanics but does NOT test the three cross-cutting correctness failure modes:

1. **Partial vec0 corpus**: A chat with some legacy `message_embeddings` rows and a few newly dual-written vec0 rows — should test that the native fast path does NOT silently return only the vec0 subset.
2. **Selective post-filters**: User/category/thread filters with matches outside the unfiltered top-K — should test that native search still returns those matches.
3. **maxMessages timestamp boundary**: Multiple messages sharing the cutoff date — should test native and numpy paths return the same candidate set.

These tests are needed in `tests/database/repositories/test_chat_search_native.py` (mock sqlProvider for partial coverage) or `tests/database/providers/test_sqlite3_vector_search.py` (real sqlite-vec with controlled data).

title: vec0 partial corpus: no backfill from existing message_embeddings, native search silently returns subset
content:
GATE 2 REVIEW FINDING: The vec0 table is populated only via dual-write in saveMessageEmbedding() for NEW messages after rollout. There is no out-of-band backfill from existing message_embeddings rows. This means:

- Chats with pre-rollout embeddings (80k+ rows in message_embeddings) and only a few hundred post-rollout rows in vec0 will have native search silently operate on the vec0 subset only.
- The caller-side `if nativeResults:` guard only handles the empty-vec0 case (returns []). A non-empty but incomplete vec0 passes the guard and returns partial results.
- There is no mechanism to detect or warn when vec0 corpus is significantly smaller than the numpy corpus for a given chat.

This is distinct from the empty-vec0 fallback issue (already documented) because: empty → fallback works correctly; partial → native path silently returns subset as if it were complete.

The fix must be either: (a) add a backfill migration to populate vec0 from message_embeddings, or (b) add a vec0 row-count vs message_embeddings row-count comparison at search time to decide whether native path is safe to use.

FILE: `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` — `_semanticSearch()` native path + `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` vec0 dual-write

title: vectorSearch() readonly search path: missing vec0 table raises → numpy fallback, never attempts DDL
content: The `vectorSearch()` method uses `readonly=True` (SQLite PRAGMA query_only blocks DDL). This means if a vec0 table hasn't been created yet for the queried dimension, the SQL error raises and triggers the numpy fallback in `_semanticSearch()`. Table creation (`createVectorTable()`) happens ONLY in the write path (saveMessageEmbedding → _upsertVecMessageEmbedding) with `readonly=False`. This separation prevents the search path from accidentally creating tables and keeps the search path safe for readonly connections.

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: avoid sqlite_vec.load(), use aiosqlite enable/load_extension/disable instead
content: The sqlite-vec extension is loaded via raw aiosqlite calls: `await db.enable_load_extension(True)` → `await db.load_extension(sqlite_vec.loadable_path())` → `await db.enable_load_extension(False)`, wrapped in try/finally. The `sqlite_vec.load(conn)` helper is deliberately NOT used because it accesses `connection._conn` (the raw sqlite3 connection under aiosqlite's async wrapper), which is fragile and bypasses aiosqlite's async safety. Extension availability is verified via `SELECT vec_version()`. The design doc originally proposed `connection.run(_load)` but aiosqlite has no `run()` method (confirmed against aiosqlite 0.22.1 source).

title: vec0 dual-write rowid fallback: if metadata-column DELETE fails, SELECT rowid → DELETE by rowid
content: The vec0 dual-write in saveMessageEmbedding() uses DELETE-then-INSERT because vec0 has no unique constraint on metadata columns (no PRIMARY KEY, implicit rowid only). The initial DELETE uses metadata columns (chat_id, message_id, model). If that DELETE doesn't uniquely identify a single row (e.g., duplicate metadata entries), a fallback approach is used: SELECT rowid from vec0 with the same metadata columns, then DELETE by rowid. This ensures single-row replacement even without a unique constraint.

title: maxMessages pre-filter joins message_embeddings (not just chat_messages) to match numpy candidate-pool semantics
content: The native vector search path computes the maxMessages cutoff (minDate) by querying `message_embeddings` (not just `chat_messages`) to match the numpy path's candidate-pool semantics. The numpy path applies maxMessages by filtering `message_embeddings` to the N most recent rows per chat. The native path mirrors this by computing `minDate` from `message_embeddings` and pushing it into the vec0 MATCH query via `filterClause date >= :minDate` (Option B pre-filter from the design). This ensures both paths rank over the same recent-N candidate set, producing comparable results regardless of whether the search hits the native or fallback path.

title: Compound filter for maxMessages: date + message_id to fix timestamp-ties precision
content:
The native vector search path (`_nativeVectorSearch()` in `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py`) originally used `date >= :minDate` as the maxMessages cutoff filter. When multiple messages shared the same timestamp (common for messages sent in the same second), messages outside the top-N but sharing the cutoff timestamp entered the native candidate pool — making native and numpy results diverge.

**Fix**: Changed the cutoff query from `SELECT c.date` to `SELECT c.date, me.message_id`, and replaced the simple `date >= :minDate` filter with a compound filter:
```
(date > :minDate OR (date = :minDate AND message_id >= :minMessageId))
```
This exactly mirrors the numpy path's `ORDER BY c.date DESC, me.message_id DESC` + `LIMIT/OFFSET` semantics, eliminating the inconsistency. Both cutoff columns (`date` and `message_id`) are returned from the cutoff query and passed as filter parameters (`minDate`, `minMessageId`).

**Test**: `test_nativeSearchWithMaxMessages` was updated to mock both `date` and `message_id` return values and assert the compound filter clause plus both filter params. Also verifies the cutoff SQL selects `c.date` and `me.message_id`.

title: vec0 partial corpus resolution: REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS chat setting triggers full re-embedding
content: The native (vec0) search path may operate on a partially-mirrored corpus during the transitional period after rollout, because pre-existing embeddings in `message_embeddings` are only dual-written to vec0 when they are re-generated. The resolution documented in code (inline comment in `_semanticSearch()`) is to enable `REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` chat setting for affected chats, which triggers a full re-embedding pass, populating vec0 via the dual-write path. This is an operational workaround, not a code-level fix — no backfill migration exists.

title: AbstractModel embedding API surface: exact inventory of members + cross-provider dimension resolution
content:
Comprehensive inventory of embedding-related members on `AbstractModel` (lib/ai/abstract.py):

**Existing members (always available on every AbstractModel instance):**
1. `supportsEmbedding: bool` — `@property`, reads `self._config.get("support_embeddings", False)`. Always available.
2. `_generateEmbeddings(text: str) -> list[float]` — `@abstractmethod`. Must be implemented by every concrete subclass. `YcAIModel` (yc_sdk_provider.py) implements it as a stub that raises `NotImplementedError` — YC SDK provider does not support embeddings.
3. `generateEmbeddings(text, *, attempts=3, consumerId=None) -> list[float]` — public async method. Always available. Raises `NotImplementedError` if `supportsEmbedding` is False, `ValueError` on empty/bad input, `RuntimeError` on retry exhaustion.

**NOT on AbstractModel:** `embeddingDimensions` is NOT defined. It only exists on `FastembedModel` (fastembed_provider.py:449) as a `@property` returning `Optional[int]`.

**Internal-only dimension config:** `BasicOpenAIModel._generateEmbeddings` reads `embedding_dimensions` from `self._config` and passes it as OpenAI's `dimensions` kwarg. This configured value is NOT exposed as a public property — no `embeddingDimensions` attribute exists on `BasicOpenAIModel` or its subclasses (`YcOpenaiModel`, `OpenrouterModel`, `CustomOpenAIModel`).

**Cross-provider dimension resolution:** `len(await model.generateEmbeddings(text))` is the only reliable, always-available way to get embedding dimensions from an arbitrary model object returned by `LLMManager.getModel()`.

**Confirmed practical usage in `_dtCronJob`:** Dimensions are never queried from the model object. The code checks `model.supportsEmbedding` then calls `model.generateEmbeddings(query)` and saves the vector. The dimension is inferred from `len(queryEmbedding)` at the DB layer via dimension-aware vec0 table naming (`vec_message_embeddings_{dimensions}` in `internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py`).

title: YcAIModel._generateEmbeddings is a NotImplementedError stub — no embedding support
content: `YcAIModel` (lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py) implements `_generateEmbeddings` as a stub that raises `NotImplementedError`. This means the Yandex Cloud SDK provider does not support embeddings at all — any code path that attempts to generate embeddings using a model from the `yc-sdk` provider will hit a `NotImplementedError`. This is intentional behavior, not a missing implementation.

title: Cleanup logic consolidated: deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings() moved to ChatEmbeddingsRepository
content: The vec0 model-change cleanup that previously lived inline in `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob()` (using provider.listTables directly + manual DELETE loops) has been moved into a new public method `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel)`. This method also extends cleanup to the `message_embeddings` table — not just vec0 tables — so stale embeddings under the old model are also purged from the authoritative table, triggering re-embedding by the backfill worker (`getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` discovers them). The method is stateless, idempotent (zero rows on the common path), and follows the same error-handling pattern as `deleteChatEmbeddings()`: outer `except Exception` swallows failures at warning level with exc_info=True so backfill continues. The vec0 portion is gated on `sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()` with a best-effort inner try/except for `NotImplementedError` from `listTables`. This consolidates all embedding-deletion logic into the repository, leaving the handler as a thin caller.

title: Stale `import datetime` in chat_embeddings.py after libUtils.now() refactor
content: The file `internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py` had an unused `import datetime` (flake8 F401) that was left over from replacing `datetime.datetime.now()` calls with `libUtils.now()` in `saveMessageEmbedding()`. The `datetime` module was no longer referenced anywhere in the file. When adding new methods, ensure any stale imports from prior refactors are cleaned up so that `make format lint` passes.

title: Reversal: in-memory model tracking reinstated for cleanup gating in _dtCronJob
content:
The model-change cleanup strategy in `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob()` was reversed again: back to in-memory tracking, but this time delegating cleanup to `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()`.

Previous evolution:
1. Original: in-memory `_prevModelByChat` dict (lost on restart, broken)
2. Previous: stateless per-tick DELETE via provider.listTables (idempotent but ran on every tick)
3. Now: `_embeddingModelTracker: Dict[int, str]` tracks `chatId -> modelKey`. Cleanup only fires when modelKey differs from stored value. Delegates to `db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel)`.

modelKey construction: `modelName` alone when no `embeddingDimensions` attribute or when it's None; `"modelName:{dims}"` when the model exposes non-None `embeddingDimensions` (e.g., FastembedModel).

Key distinction from the original broken approach: this version doesn't rely on tracking for correctness (the repo method is idempotent and safe to call) — the tracker is purely an optimization to avoid redundant work on every CRON tick. If restarted, the tracker is empty and cleanup fires once (idempotent), which is correct.

title: Pyright workaround: use getattr instead of hasattr for optional model attributes not on AbstractModel
content:
When checking for `embeddingDimensions` on a model instance (which is only defined on `FastembedModel`, not on `AbstractModel`), pyright rejects `hasattr(model, "embeddingDimensions")` + subsequent attribute access because pyright doesn't narrow types based on `hasattr`. 

Instead use: `dims = getattr(model, "embeddingDimensions", None)` — this produces identical runtime behavior (None when the attribute is absent) and pyright is satisfied because `getattr` with a default is dynamically typed and doesn't trigger the "unknown attribute" error.

Applies to any handler code that needs to conditionally access subclass-specific properties on `AbstractModel` instances.

title: Mock auto-creates attributes: must explicitly set embeddingDimensions=None for default test model mock
content:
When using `Mock()` for a model that should NOT expose `embeddingDimensions`, the Mock auto-creates `mockModel.embeddingDimensions` as a child Mock object on first access. This means `getattr(mockModel, "embeddingDimensions", None)` returns a Mock (truthy, not None), which breaks gating logic that checks `if dims is not None:`.

Fix: explicitly set `mockModel.embeddingDimensions = None` in the default test model mock. This makes `getattr` return None, correctly simulating both "attribute doesn't exist on base class" and "model hasn't probed dims yet" cases.

Another option: use `Mock(spec=AbstractModel)` which raises AttributeError for unknown attributes. However, this requires the base class to declare all accessed attributes (like `supportsEmbedding`).

Rule of thumb: when a mock should simulate "attribute does not exist", explicitly set it to `None` rather than relying on Mock's auto-creation or del.

title: Handler tests should not test repo-level concerns after delegation
content:
When a handler delegates database work to a repository method, handler tests should only test the handler-level contract (gating, argument passing), not repo-level concerns. Specifically:

1. The shared `_makeDatabase()` helper should pre-wire the new repo method as `AsyncMock()` so all tests work by default.
2. Tests that verified repo-level internals (e.g., `isVectorSearchSupported()`, `listTables()` behavior, provider fetch failures) through the handler should be removed from handler tests — those belong in the repository's own test suite.
3. Handler tests should verify: correct arguments passed to the repo method, correct gating logic (tracker prevents redundant calls), and that the method is not called on early-return paths (model missing, model doesn't support embedding).

This pattern was applied in the ChatSearchHandler refactor: old inline vec0 cleanup used provider directly, and its tests checked `provider.execute` calls with specific SQL. After delegating to `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()`, those 4 repo-level tests were removed from the handler test file, and the remaining tests check the `db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` mock instead.

title: Full config-to-SQLite3Provider wiring chain through all layers
content:
The complete chain from TOML config to SQLite3Provider instantiation passes through 4 intermediate layers with no transformation:

1. **ConfigManager.getDatabaseConfig()** (internal/config/manager.py:310-324) — returns `self.get("database", {})` raw, no key filtering or transformation.

2. **Database.__init__(config)** (internal/database/database.py:194) — passes the entire `[database]` section dict to `DatabaseManager(config)`.

3. **DatabaseManager.__init__(config)** (internal/database/manager.py:60-89) — stores the config. The `DatabaseManagerConfig` TypedDict expects `default: str`, `chatMapping: Dict[int, str]`, `providers: Dict[str, SQLProviderConfig]`.

4. **DatabaseManager.getProvider(providerName)** (manager.py:170-176) — passes `self.config["providers"][providerName]` to `getSqlProvider()`.

5. **getSqlProvider(config: SQLProviderConfig)** (providers/__init__.py:90-138) — extracts `parameters: dict = config.get("parameters", {})` and calls `SQLite3Provider(**parameters)`.

Key behavioral property: **the `parameters` dict is splatted directly into the constructor with NO filtering**. Any key under `[database.providers.N.parameters]` in TOML becomes a keyword argument. If the constructor doesn't accept it, Python raises TypeError. No transformation, renaming, or validation happens between TOML and the constructor.

This means adding a new SQLite3Provider parameter requires exactly 3 changes with no pipeline modifications:
(a) TOML defaults in `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` under `[database.providers.default.parameters]`
(b) Constructor signature + __slots__ entry in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py`
(c) Instance attribute initialization in `__init__` body

No changes needed to `getSqlProvider`, `DatabaseManager`, `ConfigManager`, or the TOML parsing pipeline.

title: SQLProviderConfig.parameters is a bare unparameterized dict
content:
In `internal/database/providers/__init__.py:86`, the `SQLProviderConfig` TypedDict defines `parameters: dict` — a bare `dict` with no key/value type parameterization (not `dict[str, Any]` or a specific TypedDict like `SQLite3ProviderParameters`).

Consequence: pyright will NOT catch typos or type mismatches in TOML parameter keys for SQLite3Provider (or any provider). A key like `dbPathe` (typo for `dbPath`) passes type checking silently and only fails at runtime with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument` when `getSqlProvider()` calls `SQLite3Provider(**parameters)`.

If strict type safety is desired, a new provider-specific TypedDict (e.g., `SQLite3ProviderParameters`) could be created and assigned to `parameters` — but this would complicate `getSqlProvider()` since the type would vary per provider. For now the system is deliberately open to accommodate all providers with the same config type.

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: self._connection is None at connect() call site
content:
In `SQLite3Provider.connect()` the `async def connect()` method has this structure:
1. Opens a new `aiosqlite.Connection` (stored in local `connection`).
2. Calls `_loadSqliteVecExtension(...)` with that local connection.
3. Sets `self._connection = connection`.

`self._connection` is still `None` during step 2. Any reference to `self._connection` at that point (e.g., passing it to `_loadSqliteVecExtension`) will pass `None` instead of a live connection, which pyright catches as `Argument of type "None" cannot be assigned to parameter "connection" of type "Connection"`. Always use the local `connection` variable for the extension-loading call.

Root cause: the agent followed instructions literally that said to use `self._connection`, but the original code used the local `connection` variable because `self._connection` hadn't been assigned yet. The fix is to use the local `connection`, which is the correct, existing pattern.

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: custom path fallback for Alpine/source-built extensions
content:
`SQLite3Provider` now supports two sources for the vec0 extension, resolved in priority order in `connect()`:

1. **pip package path** (`_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` is True): use `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` — version-matched, reliable, the default.
2. **Custom filesystem path** (`self._vectorExtensionPath` is not None): fallback when the pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux has no musl wheel, extension built from source) — accessed via the `vectorExtensionPath` kwarg on `SQLite3Provider.__init__`.

The previous logic was a simple `if _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE:` guard. The new logic decouples package availability from extension loading: the extension can be loaded even when the Python package isn't importable, as long as the compiled `.so` exists at a known path.

`_loadSqliteVecExtension()` itself was also refactored: it now accepts an `extensionPath` parameter, falling back to `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` when None. The `connect()` method determines which path to pass.

Relevant config key: `[database.providers.<name>.parameters].vectorExtensionPath`.

title: vectorExtensionPath config parameter under [database.providers.*.parameters]
content:
The `vectorExtensionPath` config parameter lives under `[database.providers.<name>.parameters]` in the TOML config, not under a separate `[database.vectorSearch]` section. It's an `Optional[str]` constructor parameter of `SQLite3Provider`.

Purpose: custom filesystem path to a prebuilt sqlite-vec shared library (`.so`/`.dylib`). When the `sqlite_vec` pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux with no musl wheel) but the extension was built from source, the provider loads vec0 from this path instead of the pip-package bundled library.

Loading priority (code at `sqlite3.py` lines 198-221):
1. If `_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` (pip package installed): use `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` (the package's bundled .so)
2. Else if `self._vectorExtensionPath is not None`: use the custom config path
3. Otherwise: skip loading, `_vectorSearchAvailable` stays `False`, numpy fallback takes over

When the config key is commented out or omitted, auto-detection via `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` (Python package) is the first-priority path.

The example in `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` (lines 46-51):
```
# Custom path to the sqlite-vec extension (.so/.dylib). Use this when the
# sqlite-vec pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux with no musl
# wheel) but the extension was built from source. When set, the provider
# loads vec0 from this path instead of the pip-package bundled library.
# Leave commented (or omit) to auto-detect via the sqlite-vec Python package.
# vectorExtensionPath = "/usr/local/lib/vec0.so"
```

title: vectorExtensionPath config example in 00-config.toml for Alpine/musl environments
content: Added a commented-out `vectorExtensionPath` example to `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` (lines 46-51) under `[database.providers.default.parameters]`, between `keepConnection` and the proxy comment block. This documents the custom path to the sqlite-vec shared library for environments where the pip package's prebuilt wheel is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux without a musl-compatible wheel). The config key `database.providers.default.parameters.vectorExtensionPath` is referenced by the sqlite-vec extension loading logic in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` to locate the .so/.dylib at runtime.

content:

content: In `ChatSearchHandler.search_command()`, the `self.llmService.rateLimit(...)` call was moved from its position before the `if keywords:` block to inside it. Filter-only searches (e.g., `/search user: @alice days: 7` with no keyword text) don't hit the embedding API or LLM, yet previously consumed the chat's LLM rate-limit budget. title: Small nitpick fixes applied: _backfillIndex bounded, lambda→_embedSync, _dtCronJob docstring renumbered
content:
Three small fixes applied during code-review cleanup of the chat-search branch:

1. **`_backfillIndex` bounded** — After `self._backfillIndex += 1`, added `self._backfillIndex %= len(enabledChats)` to keep it bounded. Python ints are arbitrary precision so no overflow risk, but cleaner.

2. **Lambda → `_embedSync` helper** — In `LocalEmbeddingsProvider._generateText()`, replaced `lambda: list(embedding.embed([text]))` with a module-level helper function `_embedSync(embedding, text)` called via `asyncio.to_thread(_embedSync, embedding, text)`. More explicit, avoids closure-variable capture fragility.

3. **`_dtCronJob` docstring renumbered** — After the `_searchEnabled` kill-switch step was removed, the numbered list in the docstring skipped from step 1 to step 3. Renumbered steps 3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 6→5.

title: Parallel subagent edits on same file require explicit reconciliation
content:
When dispatching parallel `software-developer` tasks that both modify the same file (in this case, `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py` was edited by both Group A and Group B subagents), conflicts arise. Key conflicts from this session:
- Group A removed a `_searchEnabled` kill-switch check (correct — dead code); Group B re-added it as a "bonus fix" (incorrect — misunderstood the architecture).
- The second subagent's changes can overwrite the first subagent's if both read the original and write independently.

Mitigation: avoid parallel dispatch to the same file. If unavoidable, add a dedicated reconciliation step after both batches complete to verify all changes are applied and resolve conflicts. The reconciliation should verify each intended change by reading the file state and checking for contradictions.

title: _resolveUserId @-prefix stripping bug — lookup silently fails for all chat users
content:
## Bug

`_resolveUserId()` in `ChatSearchHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py`) was stripping the `@` prefix from usernames via `clean = username.lstrip("@").strip()` and then passing the bare username to `getChatUserByUsername()`. However, the `chat_users` table stores usernames WITH the `@` prefix as the canonical format (set by `MessageSender` factories and stored as-is by `updateChatUser()`).

This meant every user lookup silently failed: `LOWER("@cthulho") != LOWER("cthulho")` → no match → warning log → `None` returned.

## Impact

- Both `/search user: @Cthulho` and the `search_messages` LLM tool (both route through `_resolveUserId`) silently failed to find any user in any chat.
- The warning log (`"/search: user %r not found in chat %d"`) was the only symptom.

## Fix

One line added after stripping and before querying (`chat_search.py:1316`):
```python
# DB stores usernames with @ prefix. Normalise to that format.
clean = f"@{clean}"
```

This handles all input forms: `@Cthulho`, `Cthulho`, `@@@Cthulho` all normalize to `@Cthulho`.

The `_resolveUserId` method is defined at line 1287.

## Regression test

`TestResolveUserId.test_resolve_without_at_prefix` — passes `"testuser"`, asserts the DB receives `"@testuser"`. Would have failed before the fix.

## Root cause chain

1. `MessageSender.fromTelegramUser()` produces `@Cthulho` (with @)
2. `saveChatMessage()` → `updateChatUser()` stores it as-is with @
3. `_resolveUserId()` strips @ → passes bare `Cthulho`
4. `getChatUserByUsername()` does `LOWER(column) = LOWER(param)` → `LOWER("@cthulho") != LOWER("cthulho")`
5. No match → returns None → warning logged

title: Test pattern: LLM tool gating tests in ChatSearchHandler — mock getChatSettings + assert error dict
content:
When testing LLM tool gating in ChatSearchHandler (ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS, EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED), the established pattern is:

## Pattern

1. **Mock `getChatSettings`** on the handler to return a dict where the relevant gate evaluates to `False`.
2. **Set up `extraData`** with a mock `EnsuredMessage` containing `recipient.id`.
3. **Call the tool handler directly** (e.g., `await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="test")`).
4. **Assert error dict** — the tool returns `{"done": False, "error": "..."}` (Russian error message, never raises).

## Example implementation

```python
class TestSearchMessagesLLMTool:
    async def test_tools_disabled(self, handler: ChatSearchHandler) -> None:
        """ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS disabled → error dict, no DB calls."""
        extraData = {"ensuredMessage": _makeMessage(recipientId=-100123)}
        mockSettings = _makeChatSettings(allowTools=False)
        with patch.object(handler, "getChatSettings", AsyncMock(return_value=mockSettings)):
            result = await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="poem")
        assert result["done"] is False
        assert "отключены" in result.get("error", "")

    async def test_embeddings_disabled(self, handler: ChatSearchHandler) -> None:
        """EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED disabled → error dict before embedding."""
        extraData = {"ensuredMessage": _makeMessage(recipientId=-100123)}
        mockSettings = _makeChatSettings(allowTools=True, embeddingsEnabled=False)
        with patch.object(handler, "getChatSettings", AsyncMock(return_value=mockSettings)):
            result = await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="poem")
        assert result["done"] is False
        assert "поиска" in result.get("error", "") or "отключен" in result.get("error", "")
```

## Helper

```python
def _makeChatSettings(allowTools: bool = True, embeddingsEnabled: bool = True) -> ChatSettingsDict:
    return {
        ChatSettingsKey.ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS: ChatSettingsValue(allowTools, "test"),
        ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED: ChatSettingsValue(embeddingsEnabled, "test"),
        # ... other required keys ...
    }
```

The helper fixture is defined in the test file and reused across test classes for `search_messages`, `list_users`, and `get_thread` tools.

## Coverage requirements

Test these gates for every LLM tool:
- Missing `extraData` / `ensuredMessage` context → error dict
- `ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS` disabled → error dict with `"отключен"` or similar
- Feature-specific gate disabled (e.g., `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` for `search_messages`) → error dict
- `getChatSettings` raises → error dict
- Repository raises → error dict
- Happy path → `{"done": True, ...}`

title: Health-check-type presence IS the restart signal — no separate `restart-on-failure` flag needed
content:
Design decision from proxy lifecycle discussion (2026-06-26): The `restart-on-failure` boolean flag was removed as redundant. The user's exact reasoning: "restart-on-failure = true parameter is useless, user have health-check-type for it."

Design principle: If you configured `health-check-type = "url"` or `"command"`, you clearly want health monitoring, and the natural response to failure is restart. The presence of a health check type IS the restart signal. If health-check-type is "none", no health checks run and no restart happens. No separate boolean gate needed.

This also eliminated `max-restarts` — health monitoring implies unlimited retries (the tunnel should always be restarted when it dies). See related memory `cc588ff4` (unlimited restart retries).

Config shape (final):
```toml
[proxy.lifecycle]
# start/stop/restart commands...
health-check-type = "url"    # "none" | "url" | "command" — no separate restart-on-failure boolean
health-check-interval = 5    # minutes
```

Design doc: `docs/plans/proxy-lifecycle-design.md` §2 (Design Goals) and §4.1.

title: Health check contract specification for proxy lifecycle
content:
Design specification from proxy lifecycle discussion (2026-06-26): Three health check types with explicit contracts:

1. **`HealthCheckType.NONE` ("none")**: No health monitoring. No CRON_JOB registered for this lifecycle. No restart triggered.

2. **`HealthCheckType.URL` ("url")**: HTTP GET request sent through the proxy to `healthCheckUrl`. The check passes if the response has a 2xx status code. Any non-2xx status, connection failure, timeout, or DNS error counts as failure. Implementation uses `httpx.AsyncClient` configured with the proxy's own `ProxyConfig.toKwargs()` to route through the proxy — this tests end-to-end connectivity (not just port liveness).

3. **`HealthCheckType.COMMAND` ("command")**: Subprocess launched via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(healthCheckCommand)`. Exit code 0 = healthy. Non-zero exit code = unhealthy. The subprocess stdout/stderr are redirected to DEVNULL (not captured). Example: `["nc", "-z", "127.0.0.1", "1080"]` for a simple TCP port check.

All three types are mutually exclusive in config. On failure: restart is triggered (if health check is configured at all — see related memory about restart-on-failure being redundant).

Design doc: `docs/plans/proxy-lifecycle-design.md` §4.2 and §5.2.

title: _formatMessageDict reverted — tests fixed to match production camelCase output, production untouched
content:
The `_formatMessageDict` method was initially "fixed" to produce snake_case keys matching its docstring, but the user **reverted that fix**. The production code remains as-is: `_formatMessageDict` delegates to `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM(..., format=LLMMessageFormat.JSON, ...)` which returns camelCase keys (`messageId`, `text`, `login`, `name`, `replyId`, `date`), drops keys with falsy values (so `replyId` is absent when None, not present-with-value-None), and does NOT produce `thread_id`.

The tests in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py` were fixed to match the actual production output instead. Key changes:
- `message_id` → `messageId` (int, not string)
- `message_text` → `text`
- `username` → `login`
- `full_name` → `name`
- `reply_id` → `replyId` (absent when None, not present-with-None)
- `thread_id` assertion removed (production doesn't produce it)

The `_llmToolSearchMessages` `formatted.append(retMsg)` fix (missing append was the real bug causing empty search results) was **kept** — only `_formatMessageDict` was reverted.

title: ProxyLifecycle commands all optional — empty command lists are no-ops
content:
All three lifecycle commands (`start-command`, `stop-command`, `restart-command`) in `ProxyLifecycleConfigDict` are optional (the TypedDict is `total=False`). When a command list is empty or missing, the corresponding method becomes a no-op:

- `start()`: empty `startCommand` → sets `_started = True` and returns immediately (no subprocess launched)
- `stop()`: empty `stopCommand` → returns immediately (no kill attempt)
- `restart()`: empty `restartCommand` → falls back to calling `stop()` then `start()` sequentially

This means you can configure a lifecycle with just `start-command` (let the OS clean up on exit), just `stop-command` (kill an externally-managed proxy), or both. A lifecycle with neither is pointless but handled without crashing — `_started` flips to True but no process runs, and health checks/restarts become meaningless.

title: Global proxy lifecycle NOT duplicated to per-service — resolveProxy creates no lifecycle for inherited configs
content:
When a service doesn't have its own `[service.proxy.lifecycle]` section, `ProxyService.resolveProxy()` returns early WITHOUT creating a new `ProxyLifecycle` instance. The service inherits the global proxy (and its lifecycle data) via `getCombined()`, but only as data on the `ProxyConfig` object — NOT as a managed process.

The effect: only `ProxyLifecycle("global", ...)` exists in `ProxyService._activeLifecycles`. All services that use the global proxy share this single lifecycle instance. There is NO per-service lifecycle duplication — one SSH tunnel, one health check schedule, one stop-on-shutdown.

title: Post-task memory hygiene: archive task-specific sections from teamlead-memory.md into memories/
content:
The user explicitly demonstrated and enforces this workflow after every completed task:

1. Review `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` — identify sections that are task-specific (narrow to one feature or subsystem) vs. durable/cross-cutting (repo-wide rules, workflow lessons, config schema).
2. Move task-specific sections into a new or existing file under `docs/llm/memories/*.md`.
3. Update `docs/llm/memories/index.md` to include the new memory file (alphabetical order).
4. Replace the moved section in `teamlead-memory.md` with a terse link pointing to the memory file.
5. Leave only truly cross-cutting or frequently-needed durable knowledge in `teamlead-memory.md`.

This keeps teamlead-memory.md lean (in practice ~100-120 lines after cleanup) and prevents drift between archived memories and the main file.

**Pre-existing trap discovered:** When older teamlead-memory.md sections have already been archived to `memories/` by a prior agent, the source sections in `teamlead-memory.md` may NOT have been cleaned up — leaving duplicate content that should have been replaced by a link. During hygiene passes, check for overlap between teamlead-memory.md sections and existing memories/ files and deduplicate.

title: Documentation drift hotspots: high-severity stale facts found across multiple docs
content:
A June 2026 documentation audit across all 12 current-state docs found several high-severity stale facts that had drifted silently:

1. **Migration version**: Multiple docs claimed 15 or 17 migrations — actual was 18. Affected: database-README.md, database-schema.md, database-schema-llm.md, developer-guide.md.
2. **Repository count**: Every doc claimed 12 repositories — actual was 14 (missing ChatSearchRepository, ChatEmbeddingsRepository, DivinationsRepository). Affected: database-README.md, database-schema.md, database-README.md, developer-guide.md, architecture.md.
3. **Phantom DDL column**: `database-schema-llm.md` documented a `created_at` column on `cache_storage` table that doesn't exist in the actual migration.
4. **Non-existent provider method**: Multiple docs (`database-README.md`, `sql-portability-guide.md`) referenced `provider.getCurrentTimestamp()` — this method has never been implemented.
5. **Incorrect method return types**: `getCaseInsensitiveComparison()` was documented as returning a SQL operator (`'LIKE'`/`'ILIKE'`) — actually returns a full expression fragment (`LOWER(column) = LOWER(:param)`).
6. **Non-existent tracking file**: `documentation-review-process.md` extensively referenced `docs/TODO.md` — this file doesn't exist; actual TODO tracking is in `/TODO.md` at repo root.
7. **`schema_migrations` table doesn't exist**: `developer-guide.md` claimed schema version is tracked in a `schema_migrations` table — it's actually tracked in the `settings` table using `db-migration-version` and `db-migration-last-run` keys.

Lesson: When updating any of these values (migration count, repository count, method signatures), systematically grep ALL .md files under docs/ — they are not independent.

title: Repository usage example consistency trap in docs
content:
During a June 2026 docs audit, a common mistake surfaced: fixing method names in a repository list table (e.g. `setCache`→`setCacheEntry`, `getChatMessages`→`getChatMessagesSince`) but forgetting to update the **usage examples** section of the same file. `database-README.md` had its repository list (lines 407-485) corrected to real method names, but its usage examples section (lines 517-657) still referenced the old names — same file, contradictory content 140 lines apart. Gate 1 caught this.

**Rule of thumb**: When correcting a method name in any documentation, search the ENTIRE file for every occurrence. Usage examples, inline code snippets, and prose descriptions all need updating.

title: database-schema.md and database-schema-llm.md are dual docs that must be updated in lockstep
content:
`docs/database-schema.md` (human-readable) and `docs/database-schema-llm.md` (LLM-optimized with DDL) document the same schema but in different formats. They share many facts (migration count, enum values, TypedDict line numbers, DDL structures) and must ALWAYS be updated together. A June 2026 audit found them 3-5 versions out of sync with each other:

- `database-schema.md` migration table said 15 but body described tables from migrations 16-18 (internal contradiction); `database-schema-llm.md` said 17 but actual was 18
- `database-schema.md` was missing enum values (`DELETED`, `USER_CONFIG_ANSWER`, `URL_CONTENT`, `URL_CONTENT_CONDENSED`) that `database-schema-llm.md` had correct
- `database-schema-llm.md` had a phantom `created_at` column on `cache_storage` DDL; `database-schema.md` was correct

AGENTS.md §Documentation Sync requires schema docs to be updated alongside schema changes, but in practice they often get out of sync with each other. When editing either file, diff against the other one.

title: Docs line-number references drift quickly — anchor on class/symbol names instead
content:
During a June 2026 documentation audit, ~30 line-number references across 10 docs/llm/ files were found stale — typically off by 10-300 lines. Worst cases: `lib/ai/abstract.py` claimed `:19` but actual `AbstractModel` class was at `:47`; `lib/ai/manager.py` claimed `:17` but `class LLMManager` was at `:49`. The pattern was consistent: docs were written at one point in time and line numbers shifted as code was added.

content:
