`ModelRunResult` (`lib/ai/models.py:838`) does NOT carry any `model` / `modelId` / `modelName` field. The class uses `__slots__` (lines 858–873), so the slot list is authoritative — no other attribute can exist on an instance. Slots: `status`, `resultText`, `result`, `toolCalls`, `mediaMimeType`, `mediaData`, `error`, `toolUsageHistory`, `isFallback`, `isToolsUsed`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `elapsedTime`. The subclass `ModelStructuredResult` (line 1108) adds only `data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]`.

The ONLY post-hoc signal of which model served is `isFallback` (bool), set via `result.setFallback(True)` inside `_runWithFallback` (`lib/ai/abstract.py:655`, guarded by `if i > 0`). It tells a caller THAT the primary was bypassed, but NOT which fallback model served.

Implications for callers of `LLMService.generateTextViaLLM` (`internal/services/llm/service.py:413`):
- When a fallback occurs mid-tool-loop, the local `model` var is reassigned to `fallbackModel` (service.py:555–557), but this is internal state — `generateTextViaLLM` returns only `ret: ModelRunResult` (line 604), never the effective model.
- The concrete winning `model.modelId` IS logged at debug/error level in `_runWithFallback` (abstract.py:645 `logger.error`, :659 `logger.debug "... succeeded on attempt"`, :663 `logger.debug "... returned error status"`), and the intended primary+fallback pair is logged in `LLMService.generateText` (service.py:813). But `generateTextViaLLM` calls the inner `generateText` with `doDebugLogging=False` (service.py:537), so only the `_runWithFallback` debug lines fire for that path.
- A caller can re-derive the candidate set by re-resolving `chatSettings[CHAT_MODEL]` / `chatSettings[FALLBACK_MODEL]` themselves, but cannot confirm which one actually won without parsing debug logs.

If a feature needs model attribution on the result (e.g., recording which model refined a user's memory), `ModelRunResult.__slots__` would need a new `modelId` slot and `_runWithFallback` would need to set it. The model object knows its own id (`AbstractModel.modelId`, exposed via `getInfo()` as `model_id`).

title: test_user_data.py autouse fixture must reset QueueService singleton too (CRON_JOB accumulation)
content:
The module-scoped autouse fixture `_resetCacheServiceSingleton` in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data.py` (lines 69–91) resets BOTH `CacheService._instance` AND `QueueService._instance`, before AND after each test.

Why QueueService too: `tests/conftest.py` resets `LLMService` / `ProxyService` / `ProxyHelper` autouse, but NOT `CacheService` or `QueueService`. Each `_makeHandler()` call constructs a `UserDataHandler` that registers a `CRON_JOB` handler on the process-wide `QueueService` singleton; without a reset these references persist across tests (and leak into other test modules that run afterward). The `CacheService` reset is needed because the singleton holds a reference to the injected database — the previous test's closed in-memory DB would leak into the next.

This is distinct from memory 814d7aa8 (CacheService reset + injectDatabase for genuine SQLite round-trip) — that covers the DB-wiring half; the QueueService reset is the additional requirement for any handler that self-registers a cron job via QueueService.

Also notable in this test file: `generateTextViaLLM` is mocked at the INSTANCE level (`handler.llmService.generateTextViaLLM = AsyncMock(...)`, borrowed from `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_dev_commands.py`), not via the singleton. The read-back assertion pattern for refinement persistence is: `userInfo = await testDatabase.chatUsers.getChatUser(...)` → `metadata = handler.parseUserMetadata(userInfo)` → inspect `metadata.get("memoryRefinement", {}).get(str(threadId))` for `summary` / `lastProcessedMessageDate` / `lastProcessedMessageId` (note: `lastRefinedTS` is in-memory only, NOT persisted — assert via `handler._lastRefinedTS.get(key)`).

title: Refinement JSONL logger design decisions — two deliberate deviations from printJSONLog
content:
Added 2026-07-06 to `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`: `_writeRefinementJsonLog` + `_resolveRefineModel`, plus `[user-memory.json-logging]` config in `configs/00-defaults/user-memory.toml`. This is the SECOND instance of the JSONL-logging pattern (first = `AbstractModel.printJSONLog` at `lib/ai/abstract.py:784`). Docs update was deferred to a separate step.

Two design decisions that DELIBERATELY diverge from `printJSONLog`:

1. **Empty summaries ARE logged.** The hook call in `_runRefinement` is placed AFTER `newSummary = (result.resultText or "").strip()` is bound and BEFORE the `if not newSummary:` early-return guard. This is the OPPOSITE of `printJSONLog`, which silently returns early on empty `resultText` (see memory ef3d8c91). Rationale: for memory-refinement debugging, knowing an empty summary was produced (and then discarded without persisting) is valuable diagnostic signal.

2. **Write wrapped in `try/except OSError`** (debug log + swallow, do NOT re-raise). `printJSONLog` has NO try/except around its `open(filename,"a")` write. Rationale: "refinement must never break over a log write" — the logging is best-effort side-channel. When replicating this pattern for NEW features, prefer the `try/except OSError` form for safety. Covers file/permission/disk errors.

Config shape mirrors `[models.json-logging]` (3 keys: `enabled` bool, `file` str, `add-date-suffix` bool). Date suffix computed via UTC `strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` to match the LLM logger. Fields logged (11): date, chatId, userId, threadId, login, messagesCount, firstMessageId, lastMessageId, summary, model, elapsedTime.

Tests: 3 in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data.py` (`TestRefinementJsonLog`): disabled-by-default, full-fields-write, empty-summary-write.

title: Resolving effective model for logging — isFallback selects primary vs fallback chat setting key
content:
Concrete implementation of the abstract strategy documented in memory 701ee56a ("ModelRunResult does NOT carry the model id"). When you need to record WHICH model served a request for logging purposes but `ModelRunResult` carries no `modelId` field, the working pattern (implemented in `UserDataHandler._resolveRefineModel`, `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`):

```python
def _resolveRefineModel(self, *, chatSettings: ChatSettingsDict, result: ModelRunResult) -> str:
    key = ChatSettingsKey.MEMORY_REFINE_FALLBACK_MODEL if result.isFallback else ChatSettingsKey.MEMORY_REFINE_MODEL
    value = chatSettings.get(key)
    if value is None:
        return ""
    return value.toStr()
```

- `result.isFallback` (bool) is the ONLY post-hoc signal of which model tier served the request (set via `setFallback(True)` in `_runWithFallback` when `i > 0`).
- Selects the feature-specific primary/fallback key pair (`MEMORY_REFINE_MODEL` / `MEMORY_REFINE_FALLBACK_MODEL`). For other features, substitute the corresponding `ChatSettingsKey.X_MODEL` / `X_FALLBACK_MODEL` pair.

NOTE on `.get()` usage: the implementation uses `.get(key)` returning `Optional[ChatSettingsValue]`, but per memories 442ede71 and fb9ccb4d, ALL `ChatSettingsKey` values are guaranteed present in the defaults dict with `ChatSettingsValue("")` fallback (from `HandlersManager.__init__`), so `chatSettings[key].toStr()` (direct indexing) would also be safe and is the project convention. The `.get()` here is harmless but technically inconsistent with convention — future code should prefer `chatSettings[key]` directly; it returns `""` (never None, never KeyError) for unconfigured keys.

Type hint: use `ChatSettingsDict` (from `internal.bot.models`), NOT `Dict[str, Any]` — it's the concrete return type of `BaseBotHandler.getChatSettings()`.

title: getChatMessagesSince returns DESC ordering — messages[0] is newest
content:
`ChatMessagesRepository.getChatMessagesSince` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_messages.py:208+`) returns messages ordered by `c.date DESC, c.message_id DESC` — i.e. **newest first**.

This means for a non-empty result list:
- `messages[0]` = the NEWEST message (highest date/message_id)
- `messages[-1]` = the OLDEST message

This is non-obvious because the method name ("Since") suggests a chronological "from this point onward" ordering (oldest first), which is the intuitive assumption. Code that indexes `[0]` expecting the oldest message (e.g. for a "firstMessageId" field) will be wrong — it gets the newest.

Verified during code review of the user-data refinement JSONL logger (July 2026). The hook in `_runRefinement` (`user_data.py`) correctly accounts for this: `firstMessageId=messages[-1]["message_id"]` (oldest), `lastMessageId=messages[0]["message_id"]` (newest). The test `_seedChatMessages` (test_user_data.py:443) seeds incremental ids 1000..1004 with ascending dates; after DESC sort, `messages[0]` has id 1004, `messages[-1]` has id 1000 — matching the hook's indexing.

Related: the result list is guaranteed non-empty at any point AFTER the `if len(messages) < self._memoryMinMessagesToRefine: return` guard (default threshold = 5), so `[0]` / `[-1]` indexing is safe downstream of that check.

title: ModelRunResult.isFallback semantics: "non-primary attempt served", NOT "fallback succeeded"
content:
`ModelRunResult.isFallback` (defaults to `False`, set via `result.setFallback(True)`) does NOT mean "a fallback model successfully produced output." It means **"the returned result came from a non-primary model attempt"** — regardless of whether that attempt succeeded or failed.

The flag is set in `AbstractModel`'s model-execution loop (`lib/ai/abstract.py:655`): when iterating over `[primary, fallback1, fallback2, ...]`, `setFallback(True)` is called for every attempt where the loop index `i > 0` (i.e. any non-primary model). The loop returns the first successful result; if all models fail, it returns `lastResult` (the last attempted).

**Edge case gotcha:** if the primary model (i=0) fails AND all fallbacks also fail, the returned `lastResult.isFallback` is `True` (because the last attempt was a fallback with `i > 0`), even though the run ultimately produced no usable output (`resultText` empty, status in `ERROR_STATUSES`).

**Impact on consumers:** code that uses `isFallback` to select which model id to report/log (e.g. `_resolveRefineModel` in `user_data.py`, which picks `MEMORY_REFINE_FALLBACK_MODEL` vs `MEMORY_REFINE_MODEL`) will report the fallback model id for a run that failed across all models. This is arguably "faithful logging" (it records which model the result came from) but it does NOT guarantee the fallback model actually succeeded.

When consuming `isFallback`, check `result.status` or `result.resultText` if you need to distinguish "fallback served successfully" from "all models failed, last was a fallback."

See also memory `dc1f4607` (isFallback is NOT a constructor param — use `setFallback()`).

title: Bare builtin generics (list[dict], dict) are Any-typed — violate "no Any" rule
content:
A subtle application of the repo's "no `Any`" rule: bare PEP 585 builtin generics like `list[dict]` or bare `dict` in type annotations are effectively `dict[Any, Any]`, which violates the rule. This was flagged as a NIT in code review of `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data.py` where `_readRefineLog` had return type `list[dict]`.

The fix is to use the `typing`-module generics with explicit key/value types: `List[Dict[str, Any]]` (importing `List`, `Dict`, `Any` from `typing`). Note this also means test files that already use `from typing import ...` should stay consistent with that style rather than mixing in PEP 585 builtins.

Context: Memory `80ff2fbc` documents that PEP 585 usage is inconsistent across the codebase, but this is the specific case where bare generics cross from "style inconsistency" into an actual "no Any" rule violation because the type parameters default to `Any`.

title: JSONL date-suffix uses UTC — test assertions must compute expected suffix via UTC
content:
Both the LLM JSONL logger (`AbstractModel.printJSONLog` in `lib/ai/abstract.py`) and the user-memory refinement JSONL logger (`UserDataHandler._writeRefinementJsonLog` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`) compute their `.YYYY-MM-DD` date suffix using UTC:

```python
datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
```

When writing tests that assert on the dated filename (e.g., globbing `refine.jsonl.*` and checking the suffix), the test MUST compute the expected suffix the same way — via `datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` — NOT via `datetime.date.today().isoformat()` or `datetime.date.today().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`, which use local time. Using local time will cause test failures or flakiness in any non-UTC timezone.

Example test pattern (from `test_refinementJsonLogWithDateSuffix`):
```python
expectedSuffix = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
datedFiles = list(tmp_path.glob("refine.jsonl.*"))
assert len(datedFiles) == 1
assert datedFiles[0].name == f"refine.jsonl.{expectedSuffix}"
```

title: Refinement JSONL logging: control-flow invariant + test conventions (post-review-fix)
content:
UPDATES memory c36c911d (which said "3 tests"). As of 2026-07-06, a Gate 1 code review found 7 issues on the refinement JSONL logging feature (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`), all were fixed, and a Gate 2 confirmation review PASSED — all 7 resolved, no regressions.

## Control-flow invariant of `_runRefinement` (3 paths) — the key gotcha
The `_writeRefinementJsonLog(...)` hook call sits at a precise position in `_runRefinement` that MUST be preserved under refactor:
1. **Exception path**: `except Exception: ... return` block runs FIRST. The hook is AFTER it, so exceptions are NEVER logged (the early-return happens before logging).
2. **Empty-summary path**: hook runs, THEN `if not newSummary: ... return`. So empty summaries ARE logged but NOT persisted (deliberate — diagnostic signal).
3. **Success path**: hook runs, THEN summary is persisted. Logged + persisted.

Moving the hook before the `except` block would log exceptions; moving it after the `if not newSummary` guard would stop logging empty summaries. Both would break the documented design.

## Double guard (defense-in-depth)
The hook call site is now wrapped in `if self._refineLogEnabled:` (added in the fix round) so that `_resolveRefineModel(...)` (eager model-id resolution) is SKIPPED entirely when logging is disabled. The method `_writeRefinementJsonLog` ALSO retains its own internal `if not self._refineLogEnabled: return` guard. This redundancy is intentional — the call-site guard prevents wasted model-resolution work; the internal guard protects against direct calls from elsewhere. Do not remove either.

## `_resolveRefineModel` uses defensive `.get()` — NOT because keys may be absent
`_resolveRefineModel` reads `chatSettings` with `.get(KEY)` (not `[KEY]`). The rationale (per the corrected docstring) is that the hook call site is OUTSIDE any try/except for KeyError — the only wrapping protection is `try/except OSError` around the file write, which does NOT cover dict access. So `.get()` ensures the hook can never raise KeyError and break refinement. Both `MEMORY_REFINE_MODEL` and `MEMORY_REFINE_FALLBACK_MODEL` DO have TOML defaults — the `.get()` is purely call-site robustness, not missing-key defense.

## Test suite now has 6 tests in `TestRefinementJsonLog` (was 3)
1. `test_refinementJsonLogDisabledByDefault` — passes `jsonLogging=None` (true omitted-sub-table default).
2. `test_refinementJsonLogDisabledWhenExplicitlyConfigured` — passes `jsonLogging={"enabled": False, ...}` (explicit disable).
3. `test_refinementJsonLogWritesAllFields` — full field write.
4. `test_refinementJsonLogWritesEmptySummary` — empty-summary logged.
5. `test_refinementJsonLogUsesFallbackModelWhenIsFallback` — calls `fallbackResult.setFallback(True)`, stubs both `MEMORY_REFINE_MODEL` + `MEMORY_REFINE_FALLBACK_MODEL` to distinct values, asserts `entry["model"]` == FALLBACK id. Drives the REAL `_resolveRefineModel` branch (not stubbed at wrong level).
6. `test_refinementJsonLogWithDateSuffix` — `add-date-suffix: True`, globs `refine.jsonl.*`, asserts exactly one file with today's UTC date. Computes expected suffix same way as writer: `datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`.

## Test-helper convention: `jsonLogging=None` vs explicit dict
`_makeUserMemoryConfigManager(jsonLogging=None)` OMITS the `json-logging` sub-table entirely (the `if jsonLogging is not None:` guard in the helper). This exercises the TRUE omitted-default path (handler sees `userMemoryConfig.get("json-logging", {})` → `{}`). This is DISTINCT from `jsonLogging={"enabled": False}` which writes an explicit disable sub-table. When testing default behavior, use `None`, not an explicit dict.

title: [models.json-logging] config is undocumented in configuration.md
content:
The `[models.json-logging]` config sub-table (used by `AbstractModel.printJSONLog` / `LLMManager._initModels` in `lib/ai/manager.py`) exists in code but has NO documentation in `docs/llm/configuration.md`. Verified 2026-07-06: a grep for `json-logging` / `json_logging` in configuration.md returns only the newly-added `[user-memory.json-logging]` subsection (line 762).

Consequence: when documenting JSONL logging config patterns, there is no existing style reference for `[models.json-logging]` in configuration.md. The agent documenting `[user-memory.json-logging]` had to follow the `[user-memory.thresholds]` table style instead. The `[user-memory.json-logging]` docs (added 2026-07-06) are now the FIRST (and only) JSONL-logging config subsection documented in configuration.md — making them the de-facto style reference for future JSONL config docs.

This is a known documentation gap, not intentional. If `[models.json-logging]` is ever documented, it should be cross-referenced from the `[user-memory.json-logging]` section and vice versa, since the two share the same 3-key shape (`enabled` / `file` / `add-date-suffix`).

title: Task objectives can embed stale convention violations — cross-check against AGENTS.md
content:
On 2026-07-06, a docs-sync task objective explicitly instructed: "do NOT run `make test`, it's not needed for doc edits per the repo convention, but if you're unsure, `make lint` is the safe gate." This directly contradicts the actual repo convention (AGENTS.md: "Always run `make test` after any changes... This is mandatory") and the formally corrected decision (memory 2cabcbbe, which reversed the old skip-for-docs exception). The agent followed the objective's instruction without flagging the contradiction, running only `make lint`.

This is the 3rd recurrence of the "skip `make test` for docs" anti-pattern:
1. Original April 2026 — team-lead decision to skip
2. Formal correction 2026-06-14 (memory 2cabcbbe) — process doc updated, AGENTS.md reinforced
3. Recurrence 2026-07-06 — propagated through objective text, not agent judgment

**Key lesson (general principle, not just about make test):** Task objectives authored by team leads are NOT authoritative sources of project convention. They can lag behind or contradict AGENTS.md updates. When an objective's instructions conflict with AGENTS.md hard rules (quality gates, naming conventions, SQL portability rules, etc.), follow AGENTS.md and flag the discrepancy in the response. Do not blindly propagate stale instructions from objectives into actions.

The specific convention: `make test` is mandatory after ALL changes including docs-only, per AGENTS.md and docs/documentation-review-process.md. Never skip it based on an objective's instruction.

title: elapsedTime vs elapsed_time: two JSONL loggers use incompatible field names
content:
The repo has TWO JSONL loggers that log elapsed LLM-call time, but they use DIFFERENT field names for the same concept — the logs are NOT field-name-compatible:

1. `AbstractModel.printJSONLog` (`lib/ai/abstract.py`, the older LLM request/response logger) writes the field as `elapsed_time` (snake_case) — predates the repo's camelCase convention.
2. `UserDataHandler._writeRefinementJsonLog` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`, the newer refinement-specific logger, added 2026-07-06) writes the field as `elapsedTime` (camelCase) — follows AGENTS.md convention for new code.

The newer camelCase choice is CORRECT per project convention (all new code is camelCase). The inconsistency exists because the older `printJSONLog` was never retrofitted.

Practical impact: any tooling/script that greps or parses BOTH JSONL files for elapsed time must handle both field names, or it will silently miss one logger's entries. The docs say the refinement log "mirrors"/"is modeled on" `printJSONLog` but don't flag this divergence (flagged as a REC in the Gate 2 review on 2026-07-06, not yet addressed).

Discovered during Gate 2 integration review of the refinement JSONL logging feature (ses_0c912201affe8bZ1JszBQUzDQk → review-only, PASS).

title: _refineLogFile empty-string fallback: enabling JSONL logging without 'file' key writes to wrong path silently
content:
In `UserDataHandler.__init__` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`), the refinement JSONL log config is read as:

```python
refineLogConfig = userMemoryConfig.get("json-logging", {})
self._refineLogEnabled: bool = bool(refineLogConfig.get("enabled", False))
self._refineLogFile: str = refineLogConfig.get("file", "")           # <-- default ""
self._refineLogAddDateSuffix: bool = bool(refineLogConfig.get("add-date-suffix", True))
```

The code fallback for `file` is `""` (empty string), NOT the documented/runtime default `"logs/user-memory-refinement-json.log"`. In normal operation this is harmless because `configs/00-defaults/user-memory.toml` always provides the `file` value, so the fallback is never hit.

BUT if a config overlay sets `[user-memory.json-logging] enabled = true` WITHOUT also setting `file` (e.g., a minimal local override that assumes defaults cascade), the behavior is:
- `_refineLogFile = ""`
- If `add-date-suffix = true` (the default): filename becomes `".YYYY-MM-DD"` — `open(".YYYY-MM-DD", "a")` SUCCEEDS, creating a hidden file in the process CWD (NOT in `logs/`). Silently wrong location.
- If `add-date-suffix = false`: filename is `""` — `open("", "a")` raises `OSError`/`FileNotFoundError`, which is caught and swallowed by the `try/except OSError` (debug log only). No file written, no visible error.

Either way, the operator gets no refinement log where they expect it and no clear error. The fix (not yet applied — noted as a NIT in Gate 2 review 2026-07-06, deemed not worth changing since the 00-defaults TOML covers it) would be to fall back to `"logs/user-memory-refinement-json.log"` instead of `""`.

Context: this is consistent with the "best-effort side-channel" contract of `_writeRefinementJsonLog` (see memory c36c911d), but it's a sharper edge than the contract implies because the failure is silent and location-wrong rather than just absent.

title: scripts/ writing conventions: shebang, sys.path shim, argparse, shell wrappers
content:
Consolidated conventions for writing a new standalone script under `scripts/` (gathered 2026-07-06 by auditing all existing scripts). These patterns are scattered across files and not centralized in AGENTS.md.

## Shebang lines (three forms, no single canonical one)
- `#!/usr/bin/env python3`  (dedoodize.py — standalone, no project imports)
- `#!/usr/bin/env ./venv/bin/python3`  (list_models.py, sandbox_bootstrap.py — imports project packages)
- `#!../venv/bin/python3`  (convert_llm_log_to_readable.py — relative)

## Module docstring
Every script has a module docstring with a `Usage:` block showing the `./venv/bin/python3 scripts/<name>.py` invocation form.

## sys.path repo-root shim (required when importing lib/ or internal/)
Scripts that import project packages (`list_models.py`, `sandbox_bootstrap.py`, `convert_llm_log_to_readable.py`) insert the repo root onto sys.path BEFORE the project imports, which are then flagged `# noqa: E402`:
```python
_REPO_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).parent.parent.resolve())
if _REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _REPO_ROOT)

import argparse  # noqa: E402
from internal.config.manager import ConfigManager  # noqa: E402
```
Scripts that stay standalone (dedoodize.py) skip this.

## Argument parsing
ALL scripts use `argparse`. None use raw `sys.argv` for flags. Example flags seen: `--config-dir` (repeatable), `--dotenv-file`, `--provider`, `--dry-run`, `-v`, `--packages`.

## Output / logging
Mixed: `list_models.py` uses `logging.basicConfig(...)` + `getLogger(...)`; `dedoodize.py` uses `print(...)`; `convert_llm_log_to_readable.py` writes to a file. No single mandated style.

## Shell wrappers (run-*.sh)
Every script that needs config/env has a paired `run-<name>.sh` wrapper with this exact shape:
```sh
#!/bin/sh
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
. "scripts/_load_env.sh"        # optional, when env/config needed
./venv/bin/python scripts/<name>.py --dotenv-file "$ENV_FILE" --config-dir ./configs/00-defaults $CONFIG_DIRS "$@"
```
NOTE: wrappers use `./venv/bin/python` (not `python3`), unlike the direct-invocation docstring form. `_load_env.sh` is the shared env loader; callers must `cd` to repo root before sourcing it.

## Existing script inventory (as of 2026-07-06)
__init__.py, _load_env.sh, aiodocker_demo.py, check_image_parsing.py, check_structured_output.py, check_tool_calling.py, convert_llm_log_to_readable.py, convert_readable_to_llm_log.py, dedoodize.py, list_models.py, README_llm_debug.md, reproduce_layout_extraction.py, reproduce_llm_dialog.py, run_llm_debug_query.py, sandbox_bootstrap.py, plus run-*.sh wrappers for each.

title: No precedent for direct sqlite3.connect in scripts/ — all DB access goes through provider layer
content:
As of 2026-07-06, a repo-wide grep for `sqlite3.connect` found ZERO hits in production code, tests, or scripts/. The only match is inside an archived design doc (`docs/archive/design/multi-source-database-architecture-v2.md:289`) inside a markdown code fence that was never adopted.

Implication: every existing script that needs DB or config access goes through the provider / `ConfigManager` layer (e.g. `list_models.py` and `sandbox_bootstrap.py` import `internal.config.manager.ConfigManager` and project services). There is no existing one-off maintenance script in this repo that takes a raw DB path as an argument and opens it directly with `sqlite3`.

This is relevant context for anyone writing a new maintenance script: bypassing the provider layer with raw `sqlite3.connect()` would be a first for this repo. Whether that's acceptable for a one-off, no-bot-spin-up maintenance script is an open design decision (the investigating user did not ask for a recommendation), but the established convention is provider-layer-only DB access.

title: Direct sqlite3.connect() is acceptable for standalone one-off maintenance scripts in scripts/
content:
RESOLVED CONVENTION (decision made 2026-07-06 via `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`). This supersedes an earlier memory that said direct `sqlite3.connect()` in scripts/ was "unprecedented" and an "open design decision."

## The decision
Raw `sqlite3.connect()` (bypassing the project's `BaseSQLProvider` / provider layer) IS acceptable for **standalone, stdlib-only, one-off maintenance scripts** under `scripts/` that take a raw DB file path as a CLI argument. Justification: such scripts must run without spinning up the bot, ConfigManager, service singletons, or the provider factory; pulling in `internal/` or `lib/` would defeat the "one-off maintenance tool that works on a cold DB file" purpose.

## The established precedent
`scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py` (the first such script) uses this shape:
- `sqlite3.connect(str(dbPath), isolation_level=None)` — autocommit mode, then manual `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK` for the write batch.
- `?` positional placeholders (NOT named `:param`). This is SQLite-only by design and explicitly does NOT need cross-RDBMS portability.
- Stdlib imports only (`argparse`, `json`, `sqlite3`, `sys`, `pathlib.Path`, `typing`). Zero `lib/`/`internal/` imports.
- Follows `scripts/dedoodize.py` styling: `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang, module docstring with `Usage::` block, argparse with `--dry-run`/`-v` flags, `print()` for output, `def main() -> int` + `sys.exit(main())`.

## What does NOT change
The project's SQL portability rules (go through `BaseSQLProvider`; use `provider.upsert(...)`, `provider.applyPagination(...)`, `provider.getTextType(...)`, `ExcludedValue`; no `AUTOINCREMENT`/`DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; portable column types; etc.) still apply UNCHANGED to ALL application/library code in `lib/` and `internal/`. The exception is narrow: standalone one-off maintenance tools in `scripts/` that operate directly on a DB file path given on the command line. Production bot code must still never call `sqlite3` directly.

title: Scripts: argparse kebab-case flags need dest="camelCase" to satisfy camelCase rule
content:
argparse auto-converts kebab-case CLI flags to snake_case `Namespace` attributes — `parser.add_argument("--dry-run", ...)` produces `args.dry_run`, which violates the project's mandatory camelCase rule (AGENTS.md). This passes `make lint` (flake8/pyright don't enforce naming on attribute access), so it is easy to miss.

Established convention (verified across multiple sibling scripts under `scripts/`):
- `--dry-run` → add `dest="dryRun"`, access `args.dryRun`  (check_image_parsing.py:595, check_structured_output.py:588, check_tool_calling.py:801)
- `--config-dir` → add `dest="configDirs"`, access `args.configDirs`  (check_image_parsing.py:568, check_tool_calling.py:774)
- Single-word flags also set `dest` explicitly for consistency, e.g. `--verbose` → `dest="verbose"`  (check_image_parsing.py:608)

When writing any new script under `scripts/`, every `--kebab-case` (and arguably every) flag must pass `dest="camelCase"` to `add_argument()`. Positional args keep their given name as dest, so `parser.add_argument("dbPath", ...)` is already camelCase and needs no dest.

Note: the older `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py` uses snake_case accesses (`args.config_dir` etc.) — it predates the convention; do not copy it. The newer `check_*` scripts are the pattern to follow.

title: Pyright: tuple element not narrowed by sibling element comparison — use cast, not assert
content:
Pyright limitation confirmed 2026-07-06 in `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`.

When a function returns a SINGLE tuple type like `tuple[_MetadataAction, dict[str, object] | None, str | None]` (NOT a discriminated union of tuple literals), pyright CANNOT narrow one element based on the value of another element. So after:

```python
action, parsed, preview = _classifyMetadata(metadata)
if action == _MetadataAction.UPDATE:
    # parsed is STILL typed `dict[str, object] | None` here — pyright does not
    # correlate `parsed` with `action` because the return type is one tuple,
    # not a union like `tuple[UPDATE, B, C] | tuple[SKIP, None, None]`.
    newMetadata = json.dumps(parsed, ...)  # ERROR: expected dict, got dict|None
```

This matters because a reviewer's claim that "once the StrEnum is in place, the action comparison narrows the type" is FALSE for a single-tuple return type. To get real narrowing you'd need a discriminated union of tuple literals; otherwise you must narrow explicitly.

**Fix: use `typing.cast`, not `assert`.** This REFINES the earlier memory (`9e8fe9f2`) which recommended `assert` for cross-function narrowing. The problem with `assert` is that it is stripped under `python -O`, silently removing both the check and the type hint pyright relied on. `cast` has no runtime effect either way but survives `-O`:

```python
newMetadata = json.dumps(cast(dict[str, object], parsed), ensure_ascii=False)
```

Rule of thumb: for narrowing that pyright can't prove from control flow (tuple-sibling correlation, cross-function invariants), prefer `cast(type, value)` over `assert isinstance(...)`. Reserve `assert` for actual runtime invariants you want checked when assertions are enabled.

title: Rewriting persisted JSON blobs: drop sort_keys=True to preserve original key order
content:
Convention for data-migration / maintenance scripts that REWRITE a subset of a persisted JSON column (e.g. removing one key from `chat_users.metadata`), confirmed 2026-07-06 in `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`.

Use `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)` WITHOUT `sort_keys=True` when you are mutating a blob you loaded from the DB. `sort_keys=True` alphabetically reorders every key, so every updated row changes in far more positions than the actual logical edit — bloating diffs, backups, and logs. By default Python dicts preserve insertion order, so omitting `sort_keys` keeps the surviving keys in their original positions and the on-disk diff reflects only the removed/added key.

Safety note: this is purely cosmetic for behaviour — production reads via `json.loads`, which is order-insensitive — so it only matters for diff-friendliness and reviewability. It does NOT apply to `lib/utils/utils.py::jsonDumps` (whose default `sort_keys=True` is intentional for canonical/normalized output like chat-settings serialization); this rule is specifically for surgical edits to existing blobs.

Contrast with existing memory `ccc296b0` / `445a359b` which document `jsonDumps` defaults — those are about the canonical serializer, not about surgical blob rewrites.

title: JSON format drift: stdlib json.dumps vs utils.jsonDumps in maintenance scripts
content:
When a standalone maintenance script (e.g. `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`) reads a JSON DB column (like `chat_users.metadata`), mutates a key, and rewrites it with stdlib `json.dumps`, the output bytes differ from how the production bot originally wrote the row.

**Production format** (`utils.jsonDumps` in `lib/utils/utils.py:108`): `ensure_ascii=False`, `sort_keys=True`, compact separators `(",", ":")`.
**Stdlib default** (`json.dumps`): separators `(", ", ": ")` (with spaces after comma and colon), `sort_keys=False` (preserves dict insertion order).

**Impact:** Semantically harmless — the bot re-parses JSON on read via `json.loads`, so content/order/values are identical. But the DB column carries cosmetic byte-level drift (extra whitespace) until the bot next rewrites that row. Anyone doing forensic byte comparison of JSON columns will see the inconsistency.

**Recommendation for future standalone scripts that rewrite JSON columns:**
- (a) Import and use `utils.jsonDumps` for consistency (requires sys.path shim / PYTHONPATH since `scripts/` standalone scripts don't import `lib/` by default).
- (b) Match the kwargs manually: `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)`.
- (c) If staying stdlib-only, document the format drift as intentional in the script's docstring — don't claim the rewrite leaves other keys "exactly as they were" (byte-identical); say "semantically identical (same keys, same values, same order)."

This was identified as a MINOR finding during code review of `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py` on 2026-07-06.

title: Maintenance scripts mirroring jsonDumps: omit default=str for fresh json.loads data
content:
Decision (from review of `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`): when a standalone/maintenance script rewrites a `chat_users.metadata` (or similar JSON column) and needs to match the production on-disk shape, mirror `lib/utils/utils.py:jsonDumps` — i.e. `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)` — but **deliberately omit `default=str`**.

Rationale: production `jsonDumps` adds `default=str` so datetime/other non-natively-serializable objects fall back to `str()`. But in a maintenance script the value being re-serialized is a fresh `json.loads()` result, which can only ever contain `dict/list/str/int/float/bool/None` — all natively serializable. Under that precondition, adding `default=str` would only ever mask a bug (an unexpected type slipping in). Surfacing such a type as a `TypeError` is preferable to silent stringification. So: compact + sorted keys YES, `default=str` NO.

This also supersedes an earlier "drop sort_keys to preserve order" instinct: the production bot itself always writes sorted+compact, so matching that keeps the column in its canonical shape and minimises drift vs. *future* bot writes (even if it produces a larger diff against the current row's possibly-stale format).

title: Maintenance scripts rewriting live columns: stop the bot first (TOCTOU clobber window)
content:
Gotcha for one-off maintenance scripts (e.g. `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`) that rewrite a column the bot also writes at runtime (e.g. `chat_users.metadata`):

The script does `SELECT` all rows early, processes them, then later `UPDATE`s them by primary key inside a single transaction. Between the SELECT and the UPDATE there is a TOCTOU window: if the running bot rewrites a row's `metadata` in between, the script's last-writer-wins UPDATE on the whole column silently clobbers the bot's newer payload. There is no per-field merge and no optimistic-concurrency check — the entire column is overwritten.

Mitigation/requirement: **stop the bot before running such scripts** (documented in the script's module docstring). Alternatively note the TOCTOU window explicitly. This applies to any maintenance script that SELECT-then-UPDATEs a column that the bot's write paths also touch. For `chat_users.metadata` specifically, the bot's writer is `CacheService.updateUserMetadata` (serializes full metadata dict via `utils.jsonDumps`, writes whole column).

title: Structured user-memories upgrade: planned direction (research done, design pending)
content:

title: vec0 virtual tables are created lazily at runtime, NOT via migrations
content:
CRITICAL gotcha for anyone planning a new vector-search feature: vec0 virtual tables are NOT created by any migration. They are created lazily at runtime on first write.

## How it works today (chat_history embeddings)

- Migration `migration_017_message_embeddings.py` creates ONLY the authoritative BLOB table `message_embeddings` (PK `chat_id, message_id`, columns: embedding BLOB, dimensions INTEGER, model TEXT, timestamps). Migration `migration_018` adds a secondary index on `(chat_id, model)`.
- The actual vec0 virtual table (`vec_message_embeddings_{dimensions}`, e.g. `vec_message_embeddings_384`) is created on first write in `ChatEmbeddingsRepository._upsertVecMessageEmbedding` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py:166-263`):
  1. Checks existence via `sqlProvider.listTables(tableName)` (line 205).
  2. If missing, calls `sqlProvider.createVectorTable(tableName, columns)` (line 207-221) with columns: `message_id TEXT`, `chat_id INTEGER PARTITION KEY`, `model TEXT PARTITION KEY`, `date TEXT`, `embedding FLOAT[{dim}] distance_metric=cosine`.
  3. The DDL is emitted by `SQLite3Provider.createVectorTable` (`internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py:576-631`) as `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {name} USING vec0(...)`.

## Implication for a new vector feature (e.g. user_memories)

- Do NOT write a migration to create a vec0 virtual table.
- DO write a migration (next number: 020) for the authoritative base table (mirroring `message_embeddings`'s shape: composite natural PK, BLOB embedding column, dimensions/model/timestamps, no AUTOINCREMENT, no DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP).
- Let the provider lazily create the vec0 table via `provider.createVectorTable(...)` on first write, exactly as `ChatEmbeddingsRepository` does.
- The sqlite-vec-specific DDL in `createVectorTable` is marked as needing review for PostgreSQL/MySQL (see comment at `chat_embeddings.py:201`). SQLite is the only wired-up backend today.

## Search path (for reference)

- `ChatSearchRepository.searchChatMessages` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py:84-189`) dispatches between native (vec0) and numpy fallback.
- Native path `_nativeVectorSearch` (line 638-823) calls `sqlProvider.vectorSearch(table=..., queryVector=..., k=topK, filterClause=..., distanceMetric=COSINE)`.
- sqlite-vec cosine **distance** is converted to similarity as `1.0 - distance`.
- Numpy fallback `_semanticSearch` (line 266-436) loads all BLOBs, decodes via `array.array("f", blob)`, computes cosine similarity in numpy.
- Dispatcher chooses native when `sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()` is True, falls back to numpy on empty results or exception.

## Embeddings generation

- Single-string API: `AbstractModel.generateEmbeddings(text) -> list[float]` (`lib/ai/abstract.py:492-538`). No batch API.
- Shared helper: `embedAndSaveMessage(ensuredMessage, modelName, db)` (`internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py:32-124`) — resolves model, generates vector, persists. Never raises.
- Model resolved per-chat via `ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL`. Default: `local/sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2` (a FastembedModel).

title: Memory summary injection: per-message JSON body, NOT system prompt
content:
The refined user summary (`userSummary`) is injected into each user message's JSON body, NOT into the system prompt. This is a non-obvious architectural decision with implications for any new memory-injection feature (e.g. episodic/semantic user memories with a latest-vs-relevant retrieval toggle).

## Current injection path

1. `HandlersManager._processMessageRec` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:1015-1020`) and `BaseBotHandler._updateEMessageUserData` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:363-378`) call `ensuredMessage.applyUserMetadata(metadata)` on every queued message before dispatch.
2. `EnsuredMessage.applyUserMetadata` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:917-948`) reads `metadata["memoryRefinement"][str(threadId)]["summary"]` and assigns it to `self.userSummary` (field at line 495).
3. `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM(format=LLMMessageFormat.JSON)` (`ensured_message.py:1170`) includes `"userSummary": self.userSummary` in the per-message JSON dict (dropped if falsy by `if v` filter at line 1172).
4. The chat-prompt-suffix (default in `bot-defaults.toml:207`) instructs the model to read `userSummary` from each message's JSON.

`self.userSummary` is read at exactly ONE place: `ensured_message.py:1170` (JSON serialization).

## The three message-construction sites (where a centralized "memories block" would go)

All build the system message from `CHAT_PROMPT + CHAT_PROMPT_SUFFIX`. None currently include a memories block:

1. **`BaseBotHandler.getThreadByMessageForLLM`** (`base.py:663-850`) — system message at `base.py:701-708`. Used by handleReply and handleRandomMessage (thread branch).
2. **`LLMMessageHandler.handleMention`** (`llm_messages.py:612-749`) — system message at `llm_messages.py:688-695`.
3. **`LLMMessageHandler.handleRandomMessage`** (non-thread branch) (`llm_messages.py:836-913`) — system message at `llm_messages.py:838-847` (adds `RANDOM_ANSWER_PROMPT`).

For a new centralized memories block, insert a `ModelMessage(role="system", content=...)` or append to `ret[0].content` right after the system message in each of these three sites.

## The memoryRefinement metadata key path

`chat_users.metadata` (TEXT column, JSON) → `memoryRefinement` (dict) → `str(threadId)` (e.g. "0" for main thread) → `{summary: str, lastProcessedMessageId: str, lastProcessedMessageDate: str}`. The `lastProcessedMessageDate` is the message cursor (ISO datetime). `lastRefinedTS` is in-memory only (see memory 8107b577).

## LLM tool pattern for new memory tools (precedent)

The existing `add_user_data` / `delete_user_data` tools (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py:214-287`) show the exact pattern:
- `async def _llmToolX(self, extraData: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], <typed params>, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]`
- `extraData["ensuredMessage"]` resolves chatId/userId context.
- Returns plain dict (e.g. `{"done": True, "key": key}`). Never raises (errors folded into `{"done": False, "error": ...}`).
- Registered via `self.llmService.registerTool(name=ToolName.X, description=..., parameters=[LLMFunctionParameter(...)], handler=self._llmToolX)`.
- `ToolName(StrEnum)` lives at `internal/bot/constants.py:24-72`.

title: Agent memory systems research — distilled design patterns for structured-user-memories
content:
Distilled from a 2026-07-06 comparative research session over 5 agent-memory systems (mem0, Letta/MemGPT, LangGraph, ChatGPT, Zep/Graphiti). This is the ACTIONABLE synthesis to inform the Gromozeka structured-user-memories design — raw per-system tables are NOT repeated here; re-dig via these sources if needed: mem0 [docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts], Letta [docs.letta.com/guides/agents/architectures/memgpt], LangGraph [docs.langchain.com/oss/javascript/concepts/memory], Graphiti/Zep [arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956, github.com/getzep/graphiti].

## Design ideas worth borrowing (for per-(chat,user,thread) + permanent/ephemeral + latest/relevant + tags)
1. **mem0's scoping trio → (chat, user, thread).** mem0 partitions by user_id/agent_id/run_id. Maps almost directly: chat_id (≈agent), user_id, thread_id/run_id (≈ephemeral session scope). Cleanest expression of the permanent-vs-ephemeral split: memories tied to thread_id = ephemeral; those tied to (chat_id, user_id) = permanent.
2. **Letta's core/archival split = the latest/relevant toggle.** "Always-injected core" = the LATEST path; "tool-searchable archival" = the RELEVANT path. Practical injection budget: mem0 top_k=3; ChatGPT ~1,200–1,400 words total cap; Letta ~2000 chars/core block. I.e. small (3–10 records / few-hundred-word budget), never the whole store.
3. **Graphiti's invalidate-don't-delete.** For permanent memories that change (classic "vegan→vegetarian" conflict), temporal validity windows beat destructive overwrites and preserve history. Achievable in a row-store with an `invalidated_at` column + "current truth" filter — no graph required.
4. **mem0's HYBRID retrieval, not vector-only.** Pure semantic misses names/IDs/recent facts. Every benchmarked system pairs vectors with BM25 keyword + a recency/temporal signal. This is exactly the "latest-vs-relevant" knob.
5. **LangGraph namespace tuples + freeform metadata** for tags, rather than a rigid category enum.

## Failure modes / anti-patterns these systems warn about
- **Dedup is the hard part.** mem0 v2 delegated every add-vs-update decision to an LLM (costly, no closed-form heuristic gating); LangGraph explicitly warns models either OVER-INSERT or OVER-UPDATE. → Plan a heuristic similarity-threshold pre-filter before any LLM merge decision.
- **Stale/conflicting permanent memories.** Solved ONLY by temporal invalidation (Graphiti) or explicit UPDATE (mem0 v2) — NEVER by append-only. Append-only accumulation (mem0 v3) pushes conflict resolution to retrieval time, accepting that.
- **Vector-only retrieval misses recent + exact.** All benchmarked systems add keyword (BM25) + recency/temporal signals on top of vectors.

## Consensus on tags/categories & injection count
- **Tags: freeform tags/metadata + optional entity extraction; NO system imposes a fixed predefined category enum.** (Graphiti ALLOWS prescribed Pydantic types but doesn't REQUIRE them.) Letta has no tags at all (freeform text blocks); ChatGPT surfaces a flat list with no tags.
- **Injection count: small — top 3–10 records, or a few-hundred-word token budget.** Never inject the whole store. Auto-inject a small "latest/core" set; leave the rest to tool-based search (Letta's model).

## Note on mem0 internals (the v2→v3 dedup shift)
- **v2 "Update phase":** each candidate fact compared to top-N similar memories by cosine similarity; LLM picks ADD / UPDATE (merge) / NOOP (redundant) / DELETE (irrelevant).
- **v3 (Apr 2026):** single-pass ADD-only extraction — one LLM call, no UPDATE/DELETE; memories accumulate with temporal metadata so retrieval can answer "preferred X 6 months ago" vs "prefers now". Trades correctness-on-update for lower write latency.
Both `update`/`delete` primitives remain app-callable in v3 for explicit corrections.

title: User Memories Feature: codebase anchors (planning phase)
content:
Planning a new structured user-memories feature (per-(chat,user,thread) memories + vec0 search + add/delete/search tools + permanent/ephemeral split + latest-vs-relevant toggle). Verified codebase anchors, 2026-07-06:

- **Two parallel memory systems already exist:** (1) `user_data` table (migration_001, PK `(user_id, chat_id, key)`) + `add_user_data`/`delete_user_data` LLM tools = durable permanent facts (key-value); (2) `memoryRefinement[threadId].summary` rolling bio = JSON blob in `chat_users.metadata`. The new feature unifies/replaces these.
- **vec0 tables are NOT created by migrations** — created lazily at runtime via `provider.createVectorTable(tableName, columns)`. Migration 017 only created the authoritative `message_embeddings` BLOB table; the `vec_message_embeddings_{N}` virtual table appears on first write in `ChatEmbeddingsRepository._upsertVecMessageEmbedding` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py:166-263`). Pattern to copy: migration creates relation+BLOB table; vec0 is runtime.
- **Reusable provider vector abstraction** (`internal/database/providers/base.py` + sqlite3.py): `isVectorSearchSupported()`, `vectorSearch(table, vectorColumn, returnColumns, queryVector:bytes, k, filterClause, filterParams, distanceMetric=COSINE)`, `createVectorTable(tableName, list[VectorColumnDef])`, `listTables(likePattern)`. Types: `VectorColumnType`, `VectorColumnDef` TypedDict, `VectorDistanceMetric.COSINE`, `VectorSearchResult`. SQLite path fully implemented; PG/MySQL providers not yet selectable.
- **Embeddings:** per-chat `ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL` setting (default `local/sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, 384-dim). `AbstractModel.generateEmbeddings(text)` is single-string, single-vector (no batch API); callers loop. Default embedding-model config at `configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml:131`. Shared helper `internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py:32-124` (`embedAndSaveMessage`).
- **chat_history search repo** (the pattern for memory search): `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py::ChatSearchRepository.searchChatMessages` — dispatcher picks native vec0 path (`_nativeVectorSearch`, chat_search.py:638-823) when `isVectorSearchSupported()`, else numpy fallback (`_semanticSearch`, 266-436). cosine distance→similarity = `1.0 - distance`.
- **LLM tool registration:** `LLMService.registerTool(name, description, [LLMFunctionParameter(...)], handler=self._llmTool*)` in handler `__init__`, gated by feature flag. `LLMFunctionParameter(name, description, type:LLMParameterType, required=False, extra={})` at `lib/ai/models.py:175-216`. `LLMParameterType(StrEnum)`: STRING/NUMBER/BOOLEAN/ARRAY/OBJECT. `ToolName(StrEnum)` at `internal/bot/constants.py:24-72` (existing: ADD_USER_DATA, DELETE_USER_DATA, SEARCH_MESSAGES). Handler sig: `async def _llmTool*(self, extraData, params..., **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]` returning `{"done": bool, ...}`; never raises; chat context via `extraData["ensuredMessage"]`.
- **Three system-message construction sites** (where a "memories block" would inject): `BaseBotHandler.getThreadByMessageForLLM` (`base.py:701-708`, system msg = CHAT_PROMPT+CHAT_PROMPT_SUFFIX), `LLMMessageHandler.handleMention` (`llm_messages.py:688-695`), `LLMMessageHandler.handleRandomMessage` (`llm_messages.py:838-847`). Currently `userSummary` rides per-message in JSON via `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` (ensured_message.py:1170), NOT in system prompt. A centralized memories block = new `ModelMessage(role="system")` or append to `ret[0].content` right after these assemblies.
- **Current memory refinement hooks** (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`): `_runRefinement` (472-618) persists `chat_users.metadata.memoryRefinement[str(threadId)] = {summary, lastProcessedMessageId, lastProcessedMessageDate}` under `cache.chatUserMetadataLock()`. `_dtCronJob` (301-470) every 60s, single global `_refineLock`. Prompts read from chat settings (MEMORY_REFINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT/MEMORY_REFINE_USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE), default text at `bot-defaults.toml:347-373`. Refinement LLM already gets useTools={ADD_USER_DATA, DELETE_USER_DATA, SEARCH_MESSAGES, GET_CURRENT_DATETIME}.
- **chatSettings 4-site pattern** (per add-chat-setting skill): (1) `ChatSettingsKey(StrEnum)` at `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:281-452`; (2) `_chatSettingsInfo` dict at chat_settings.py:615 (TypedDict ChatSettingsInfoValue: type/short/long/page); (3) default in `configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml [bot.defaults]`; (4) consumer reads via `chatSettings[KEY].toBool()/.toStr()/.toInt()`. Simplest boolean example end-to-end: EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED (enum :435-436, info :1107-1112, toml :128, consumers chat_search.py:339-346/498).
- **Latest migration = 019** (migration_019_add_webhook_updates_table). Next = **020**.
- **Plan docs** live in `docs/plans/<feature>-vN.md` (current residents: memory-refine-plan-v0/v1.md, random-answer-context-v1.md, python-sandboxing-v1.md, user-info-cache-plan-v1.md, llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md).
- **Research synthesis (mem0/Letta/LangGraph/ChatGPT/Graphiti):** permanent/ephemeral = Letta core/archival; latest/relevant = mem0 hybrid (vector+recency, never vector-only). Dedup = the hard part (mem0 v2 LLM-merge costly, v3 append-only+temporal, Graphiti invalidate-don't-delete). Consensus: freeform tags not enum; inject 3-10 records not whole store. Scoping trio maps to (chat_id, user_id, thread_id).

title: One-off maintenance scripts need no doc updates unless they support a recurring documented workflow
content:
Precedent established when evaluating whether adding `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py` (a standalone, stdlib-only, untested, one-off maintenance tool targeting `chat_users.metadata`) required documentation updates. Verdict: NO doc surface needed updating. This clarifies how to apply the `update-project-docs` skill's "New script" decision-matrix row.

## Decision-matrix interpretation for one-off maintenance scripts

The "New script" row says: *"Update `docs/llm/tasks.md` if it supports a documented workflow"* (e.g. `check_structured_output.py` is referenced from §4.5's schema-probe workflow). Key clarifications derived from this evaluation:

1. **"Workflow" means a *recurring* procedure referenced from `tasks.md` §4.x** — NOT a one-off cleanup. A one-off script that targets a single documented data contract does not qualify.

2. **`tasks.md` §3 (gotchas) holds code-level/data-level pitfalls** (shallow-merge, cache desync, cursor bugs), NOT operational-procedure warnings. Ops warnings like "stop the bot first" belong in the **script's own module docstring** where the operator will actually read them at run time — not in `tasks.md`.

3. **`docs/developer-guide.md` does NOT maintain a scripts index.** It only references setup-procedure scripts (e.g. `sandbox_bootstrap.py`). Do not add one-off maintenance tools there.

4. **No `scripts/README.md` index exists** (only `scripts/README_llm_debug.md`, which is scoped to LLM-debug scripts). Do NOT create a general scripts index — the skill forbids creating unsolicited doc files.

5. **The data contract the script targets need not be re-documented.** For `clear_memory_refinement.py`, the `metadata.memoryRefinement` convention was already thoroughly canonical across all schema docs (`database.md`, `database-schema.md`, `database-schema-llm.md`), ADR-014, `handlers.md`, `configuration.md`, `services.md`, `tasks.md` §3, `memories/user-memory-refinement.md`, and `teamlead-memory.md`. Adding a script that mutates an already-documented contract does not require touching those docs.

## Convention for the scripts themselves (confirmed pattern)

One-off maintenance scripts follow this shape: stdlib-only (`argparse`/`json`/`sqlite3`, NO project imports), positional DB-path arg, `-n/--dry-run` and `-v/--verbose` flags, `dest="dryRun"` on the argparse flag to keep `args.dryRun` camelCase, explicit `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` transaction discipline, and a TOCTOU "stop the bot first" warning in the module docstring.

## Threshold summary

Add documentation for a new script ONLY if it: (a) supports a recurring workflow referenced from `tasks.md` §4.x, OR (b) is part of a setup/dev procedure documented in `developer-guide.md`, OR (c) introduces a new data contract / config key / architectural decision. A one-off maintenance tool that mutates an already-documented contract clears none of these — no doc update.

title: User Memories Feature design decisions
content:
User design decisions for the user-memories feature (locked 2026-07-06, will be encoded in docs/plans/user-memories-v1.md):

1. UNIFY NOW — single new user_memories table with permanent BOOLEAN column. Migrate existing user_data rows in (as permanent type=fact memories). Retire add_user_data/delete_user_data LLM tools (replaced by add_memory/delete_memory). Rolling bio (chat_users.metadata.memoryRefinement[threadId].summary) -> a permanent memory with type=bio. Bigger one-time migration + prompt rewrite; cleanest long-term.

2. Always-in + toggle — permanent memories (capped ~10, oldest-trimmed if over) injected every message as a system block. Non-permanent follow latest-vs-relevant toggle (5). Letta core/archival split. User explicitly confirmed: "permanent added to each message".

3. Search + add at chat-time — main chat LLM gets search_memories AND add_memory (so it can remember things the user explicitly states). delete_memory is refinement-only (avoids runaway self-deletion).

4. Tags + type enum — freeform tags (set of strings, searchable) + a MemoryType StrEnum discriminator: bio/preference/fact/event/relationship. Research consensus: freeform tags (not rigid taxonomy) + light type aids filtering.

5. Similarity + LLM merge dedup — add_memory handler cosine-searches same-scope existing memories; >0.95 = duplicate (no-op), 0.85-0.95 = "similar_exists" signal returned to refinement LLM (it decides delete+readd or skip), <0.85 = insert. Heuristic gate before any LLM round-trip (mem0 v2 style; controlled cost). Thresholds MEMORY_DEDUP_DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD=0.95, MEMORY_DEDUP_SIMILAR_THRESHOLD=0.85.

Also locked (my recommendations, user did not object):
- Hybrid retrieval (vector cosine + recency tiebreak), not pure vector.
- Reuse EMBEDDING_MODEL chat setting for memory embeddings (no separate key).
- vec0 table vec_user_memories_{dim} created lazily at runtime (matches chat_embeddings pattern); migration 020 only creates relation + BLOB tables.
- "Relevant" query = embed current user message text, top-5 cosine scoped to (chat_id, user_id, thread_id), recency tiebreak. Requires EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED; silently falls back to latest if off.

title: App-generated IDs use uuid4, not ULID — instruction "ULID" diverges from codebase convention
content:
Repo-wide convention: app-generated unique IDs use `uuid.uuid4()` (stdlib), NOT ULID. Confirmed across subsystems:
- `delayed_tasks.id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL` — ID generated app-side with `uuid.uuid4()` (migration_001).
- Sandbox run IDs use `str(uuid.uuid4())` (36 chars, hyphenated); container names use `uuid.uuid4().hex` (see memory 64999b10).

There is NO `ulid` / `python-ulid` package in `requirements.direct.txt` or `requirements.txt`. Adding ULID would require a new pinned entry in `requirements.direct.txt` (under `# Runtime`) per AGENTS.md rules.

GOTCHA: a task spec may instruct "app-generated ULID" (observed 2026-07-06 in the user-memories-v1 plan authoring task — the spec said "memory_id TEXT NOT NULL (app-generated ULID)"). This conflicts with the established convention. Recommend using `str(uuid.uuid4())` for any new TEXT PRIMARY KEY IDs for consistency, and flag the divergence as a [DESIGN CHOICE] in the artifact rather than silently introducing a new dependency. The composite-natural-key strategy (PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, user_id, ...)) remains the FIRST preference per AGENTS.md; uuid4 is the fallback only when a single synthetic ID is genuinely needed.

title: Gotcha: LLM tool handler parameters are snake_case — exception to camelCase rule
content:
LLM tool handler method parameters that correspond to tool-exposed params are snake_case, NOT camelCase. This is an explicit, intentional exception to AGENTS.md's mandatory camelCase rule ("camelCase for variables, args, fields... snake_case is WRONG even though it's idiomatic Python").

WHY: The dispatch in `LLMService` calls `tool.function(extraData, **toolCall.parameters)` where the keys of `toolCall.parameters` are the exact `LLMFunctionParameter.name` strings sent over the wire to the LLM as JSON Schema property names. The handler method kwargs must match those name strings exactly. Existing tools consistently use snake_case for both the `LLMFunctionParameter.name` and the handler kwarg.

VERIFIED EXAMPLES:
- `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages(self, extraData, query="", limit=5, max_age_days=None, user_name=None, thread_message_id=None, **kwargs)` at internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:451 — note `max_age_days`, `user_name`, `thread_message_id`.
- `_llmToolSetUserData(self, extraData, key, data, **kwargs)`.

RULE OF THUMB when adding a new LLM tool: the `LLMFunctionParameter(name=..., ...)` name string AND the matching handler method kwarg must BOTH be snake_case and must match exactly. Everything else in the file (locals, helper method names, field names) stays camelCase per AGENTS.md.

The `extraData: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` first positional arg and the `**kwargs: Any` catch-all are part of the dispatch contract and are NOT tool params (camelCase-irrelevant). See memory b734e870 for the full handler signature pattern (return type, kwargs rationale, etc.).

Trigger context: designing the user-memories `add_memory`/`delete_memory`/`search_memories` tools — params like `memory_id` must be snake_case, not `memoryId`.

title: Design recommendation: vec_user_memories vec0 table should include model as a partition key
content:
For the user-memories feature (docs/plans/user-memories-v1.md, planning as of 2026-07-06), the vec0 virtual table `vec_user_memories_{dim}` should include `model` as a PARTITION KEY (or at minimum a vectorSearch filter), mirroring the proven chat_embeddings precedent — NOT just `chat_id` + `user_id` as the worked-out design specified.

THE GAP: The worked-out design in the plan brief omitted `model` from the vec0 partition keys (proposed columns: memory_id, chat_id, user_id [partition], thread_id, permanent, type, embedding FLOAT[dim]). But chat_embeddings uses `chat_id` + `model` as partition keys precisely to handle model drift. For user memories, per-(chat,user) isolation REQUIRES user_id as a partition key too, so the faithful mirror is partition keys = (chat_id, user_id, model), with dimension in the table name (vec_user_memories_{dim}).

WHY IT MATTERS: vec0 tables are dimension-scoped by table name, but two different embedding models can share the same dimension (e.g. two 384-dim models). If the EMBEDDING_MODEL chat setting changes to a same-dimension-but-different model, searchMemories would rank against STALE embeddings from the old model unless `model` is a partition key / filter. Including model makes the filter `chat_id=:chatId AND user_id=:userId AND model=:modelName` both correct and efficient (partition-key path).

The searchMemories and findSimilarMemories repository methods both take a `modelName` param already — wire it into the vectorSearch filterClause. The user_memory_embeddings BLOB table (mirroring message_embeddings) also stores model+dimensions per row for staleness detection.

NOTE: This is a [DESIGN CHOICE] flagged during plan authoring to catch a gap in the locked worked-out design. If the user overrides it in review, fall back to chat_id+user_id partition keys and accept the same-dimension-model-drift risk (track as future work alongside an embeddings-regeneration cron). sqlite-vec partition keys are SQLite-specific; PG/MySQL porting is already flagged as required future work for the whole feature.

Related existing memories: vec0 dimension-aware naming (a8af72fc), vec0 dynamic creation (94f75971), dual-write pattern (8d0a9879), createVectorTable partition-key-on-metadata gotcha (64882cfa — note partition key must only be on metadata columns, never the VECTOR column itself).

title: Tool availability is per-call (useTools), NOT per-registration-site — exclude refinement-only tools explicitly
content:
**Gotcha discovered 2026-07-06 during the user-memories plan review.**

Tool REGISTRATION is global on the `LLMService` singleton (`registerTool` adds to the shared `toolsHandlers` dict). Tool AVAILABILITY is controlled per-call by the `useTools` parameter. The existing memory `e3f8c17f` documents the mechanics (`_resolveTools`, the "default" sentinel, `useTools.get(toolName, defaultEnabled)`). The NON-OBVIOUS IMPLICATION:

The chat-time LLM call (`LLMMessageHandler._sendLLMChatMessage`, `llm_messages.py:274-288`) resolves `useTools = {TOOLS_DEFAULT_DICT_KEY: True}` when `USE_TOOLS` chat setting is on. This wildcard enables **EVERY** registered tool — including any tool registered by ANY handler's `__init__`, regardless of which handler "owns" it.

**Consequence:** If you want a tool to be "refinement-only" (available to background/refinement LLM calls but NOT to the main chat LLM), you CANNOT achieve this by choosing a "refinement-only registration site" — registration is global. You MUST explicitly disable it in the chat-time `useTools` dict:
```python
useTools[ToolName.DELETE_MEMORY] = False  # exclude from chat-time
```
This works because `_resolveTools` does `useTools.get(toolName, defaultEnabled)` — an explicit `False` overrides the wildcard `True` default (verified in `tests/services/llm/test_use_tools.py`).

**Evidence:** `grep "registerTool" internal/bot/common/handlers/` shows `LLMMessageHandler` (`llm_messages.py`) registers ZERO tools. Yet `SEARCH_MESSAGES` (registered by `ChatSearchHandler` at `chat_search.py:204`) is available to both the refinement LLM (explicit dict at `user_data.py:559-564`) AND the chat LLM (wildcard at `llm_messages.py:278`) — because registration is global.

**Rule of thumb:** To restrict a tool to a subset of LLM calls, control it via the `useTools` dict at each call site, never via registration site.

title: ModelRunResult exposes toolUsageHistory (full sequence) + toolCalls (final turn) — derive per-tool counts from toolUsageHistory
content:
`ModelRunResult` (`lib/ai/models.py:838-946`) — the return type of `LLMService.generateTextViaLLM()` — has two tool-related fields:

- **`toolCalls: List[LLMToolCall]`** — the tool calls from the FINAL assistant turn only. Not an aggregate.
- **`toolUsageHistory: Optional[Sequence[ModelMessage]]`** — the FULL multi-turn message sequence including all assistant messages with their `toolCalls`, tool-result messages (role="tool"), etc.

`LLMToolCall` (`lib/ai/models.py:552-556`) carries `.name` (the tool name string), `.id`, and `.parameters`.

**To derive per-tool call counts across the whole multi-turn run:** walk `result.toolUsageHistory`, for each assistant `ModelMessage`, collect `tc.name` across `msg.toolCalls`, accumulate per name. This gives accurate counts (e.g. `addCount`, `deleteCount`, `searchCount`).

**Caveat:** Tool RETURN VALUES (e.g. an `action: "similar_exists"` field returned by a tool) are NOT cleanly exposed. Recovering them requires parsing the `role="tool"` result-message payloads from `toolUsageHistory`, which is fragile. If you need per-return-value telemetry, prefer having the tool handler log it directly rather than post-hoc mining the result object.

title: ChatMessageDict uses 'score' not 'similarity' for cosine rank
content:
`ChatMessageDict` (internal/database/models.py:157-160) names its semantic-rank field **`score`**, NOT `similarity`. Type is `NotRequired[float]` (the only non-required field; the class is otherwise `total=True`). `NotRequired` imported from `typing` at models.py:10.

Semantics (docstring at :159):
- Semantic search path: populated with cosine similarity `1.0 - distance`. Native vec0: computed at chat_search.py:785 (`scoreByMessageId[mid.asStr()] = 1.0 - vr["distance"]`), written into each dict at `_fetchSearchResultRows` chat_search.py:626 (`rowDict["score"] = scoreByMessageId.get(mid.asStr(), 0.0)`). Numpy fallback: topScores built at chat_search.py:424, written at :626.
- Filter-only path (`_filterOnlySearch`, chat_search.py:256): **sets `score = 0.0` explicitly** — so within the search repo, filter-only results DO carry `score` (always 0.0).
- Absent ONLY on rows from other repo methods (getChatMessageByMessageId, getMessageThread, getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings) which never touch `score`. Since `score` is `NotRequired`, `dbUtils.sqlToTypedDict` leaves it off.

Gotcha: a plan draft referenced this field as `similarity` — that name does not exist. Any new TypedDict mirroring this pattern (e.g. UserMemoryDict) should name the field `score: NotRequired[float]` and follow the populate-as-0.0-or-`1.0-distance` convention.

title: Embeddings regeneration is a single path, not a separate loop
content:
The chat-history embedding "regeneration on model drift" feature is NOT a separate regeneration path. The SAME `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` (internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:284-445) handles BOTH initial backfill (never-embedded rows) AND model-drift regeneration (rows embedded under a different model). The two cases are distinguished only by the `modelName` argument flowing through.

Full mechanism (step-by-step, anchors as of 2026-07-07):
1. Discovery: `listChatsBySetting(key=ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED)` (chat_search.py:339), values filtered via `.toBool()` (:345). EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED is the discovery key (NOT REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS, which defaults true so is rarely persisted).
2. Round-robin: `chatId = enabledChats[self._backfillIndex % len]` (:354), index advances (:355-356). One chat per tick.
3. Per-chat gate: `if not chatSettings[REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS].toBool(): return` (:364-366).
4. Model resolution: `modelName = chatSettings[EMBEDDING_MODEL].toStr()` (:368); `llmService.getLLMManager().getModel(modelName)` (:371); require `model.supportsEmbedding` (:372-373).
5. **Drift cleanup (the actual mechanism)**: `currentDims = await model.getDimensions()` (:382); `modelKey = f"{modelName}:{currentDims}"` (:383-385); tracked per-chat in `self._embeddingModelTracker` (:386). Only when tracker differs, calls `self.db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel=modelName, currentDimensions=currentDims)` (:394-398). This DELETE (chat_embeddings.py:337-464) removes rows where `model != currentModel OR dimensions != currentDimensions` from `message_embeddings` AND all `vec_message_embeddings_{N}` tables. Idempotent — no-op when model unchanged.
6. **Stale detection query**: `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings(chatId, limit=_reindexBatchSize, modelName=modelName)` (chat_embeddings.py:466-550). SQL uses a `NOT EXISTS` correlated subquery (chat_embeddings.py:516-532) with `AND (:modelName IS NULL OR me.model = :modelName)`. The `me.model = :modelName` clause makes a model swap surface "missing" rows (old-model rows no longer satisfy NOT EXISTS) → returned for re-embedding. THIS is the entire drift-detection.
7. Re-embed write loop: `embedAndSaveMessage(ensuredMessage, modelName=modelName, db=self.db)` (:430-434), `await asyncio.sleep(BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS)` (:436). Per-row failures swallowed.

Re-embed write path: `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.saveMessageEmbedding(chatId, messageId, embedding, model, *, date=None) -> bool` (chat_embeddings.py:72-164), uses `provider.upsert(table="message_embeddings", conflictColumns=["chat_id","message_id"], updateExpressions={embedding, dimensions, model, updated_at: ExcludedValue()})`.

Constants: BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=50 (chat_search.py:69, fallback only — TOML default is 100); BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS=0.1 (:77). Cron registration: `registerDelayedTaskHandler(CRON_JOB, self._dtCronJob)` (:201). TOML section: `[search-history.embeddings].reindex-batch-size` (search-history.toml:7-10).

REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS is NOT auto-reset — user must toggle via /settings (docstring :322-324).

content:
