  - `_handleConfigAction_TopicSelected`, `_handleConfigAction_NextPage`, `_handleConfigAction_PrevPage` read `ButtonDataKey.Tag` from payload and thread it through.
  - `TagFilter` arm added to the dispatcher.
  - New constant `KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_TAG_FILTER_FETCH_LIMIT = 200`.

## Resolution of the Phase 5a byte-budget warning (memory 987d9f5f)
987d9f5f left an open warning: "Do NOT assume there's room to add more fields to memory-bearing payloads." Phase 5b resolved this by SPLITTING which buttons carry the tag:
- **Tag IS carried on** NextPage/PrevPage/TagFilter buttons: these do NOT carry the 32-char UUID `memoryId` (only the ≤11-char type string), so they have ~25 bytes of headroom. Verified: `{c:-1001234567890,d:np,k:relationship,p:0,tg:work}` ≈ 47 bytes. ✓ FITS.
- **Tag is NOT carried on MemorySelected buttons**: `{c:<chatId>,d:ms,k:<32hex>,p:0}` is already ~60 bytes for supergroups; adding `,tg:<tag>` overflows the 64-byte ceiling. CONSEQUENCE: viewing a memory detail and returning DROPS the tag filter (returns to unfiltered list). This is an accepted v1 limitation, documented in code comments. The suggested mitigation (user-state cache instead of payload) was NOT adopted — kept the wizard stateless.

title: searchMemories tags post-filter runs AFTER SQL offset — breaks pagination; fix with Python-side pagination
content:
GOTCHA + FIX (Phase 5b, 2026-07-07). `searchMemories` in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py` applies the `tags` filter as a **Python post-filter AFTER the SQL `LIMIT ... OFFSET ...`** (see lines ~740-742: `results = [r for r in results if requestedTags & set(r.get("tags") or [])]`). A code comment (~lines 733-739) said this was "acceptable for the admin wizard (tags filter is Phase 5b)". **This assumption was WRONG for real pagination.**

## The bug
When a tag filter is combined with a non-zero SQL offset, the page boundary straddles trimmed rows. Example: user has 20 memories, 5 tagged "work", scattered across positions 2,7,9,15,18. Fetching `limit=9, offset=0` returns the first 9 ordered by updated_at, then the tag post-filter trims to the ~3 tagged ones in that window. Fetching `offset=8` returns positions 8-16, trims to a different ~2. The user sees inconsistent/missing pages — "Next" can show fewer items or skip tagged rows entirely.

## The fix (in `_renderMemoryList`)
When a tag filter is active, do NOT use the existing SQL-offset path. Instead fetch a generous batch at offset 0 and paginate the filtered result in Python:
```python
if tag:
    # SQL offset + tags post-filter interact badly; fetch a generous
    # batch at offset 0 and paginate the filtered result in Python.
    allFiltered = await searchMemories(chatId, userId, None, type=typeForQuery,
        tags=[tag], threadId=None, limit=KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_TAG_FILTER_FETCH_LIMIT, offset=0)
    hasNext = len(allFiltered) > offset + KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE
    pageMemories = allFiltered[offset : offset + KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE]
else:
    # Existing path: SQL-level pagination via limit=PAGE_SIZE+1
    memories = await searchMemories(..., limit=PAGE_SIZE+1, offset=offset)
    hasNext = len(memories) > PAGE_SIZE
    pageMemories = memories[:PAGE_SIZE]
```
`KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_TAG_FILTER_FETCH_LIMIT = 200` — enough for realistic single-user tag pools; edge case >200 tagged memories would silently truncate (documented).

## Key lesson
Any post-SQL filter (tags, or future free-text filters) combined with SQL-level offset produces wrong pagination. The generic fix pattern: when a post-SQL filter is active, fetch a larger batch at offset 0 and paginate in Python. The `searchMemories` contract was deliberately NOT changed (the LLM `search_memories` tool doesn't paginate).

title: PayloadDict invariance: explicit Dict[ButtonDataKey, ...] annotation fails pyright — use untyped dict literals
content:
PYRIGHT GOTCHA (Phase 5b, 2026-07-07). When building a `CallbackButton` payload dict that uses `ButtonDataKey` enum members as keys, do NOT annotate the dict explicitly as `Dict[ButtonDataKey, int | str]` (or similar). Pyright rejects it:

```
ERROR: Argument of type "Dict[ButtonDataKey, int | str]" cannot be assigned to
parameter "payload" of type "PayloadDict"
  "Dict[ButtonDataKey, int | str]" is not assignable to
  "Dict[str | int, str | int | float | bool | None]"
  Type parameter "_KT@dict" is invariant, but "ButtonDataKey" is not the same as "str | int"
```

## Root cause
`PayloadDict` (in `internal/bot/common/models/keyboard_button.py` / `lib/utils/utils.py:18`) is defined as `Dict[str | int, str | int | float | bool | None]`. Dict key types are **invariant** in Python's typing system. `ButtonDataKey` (a `StrEnum`) is a subtype of `str`, but invariance means `Dict[ButtonDataKey, ...]` is NOT assignable to `Dict[str | int, ...]` even though `ButtonDataKey` <: `str`.

## Fix
Do NOT annotate the dict. Use an untyped dict literal — the existing code throughout the wizard does this and pyright infers the keys as `ButtonDataKey | str | int` literals, which widen correctly:
```python
# WRONG — triggers invariance error:
payload: Dict[ButtonDataKey, int | str] = {ButtonDataKey.UserDataConfigAction: ..., ...}

# RIGHT — untyped literal, matches existing pattern:
payload = {
    ButtonDataKey.UserDataConfigAction: ButtonUserDataConfigAction.TopicSelected,
    ButtonDataKey.ChatId: chatId,
    ...
}
```
If you must annotate (e.g., for a helper return type), use the `PayloadDict` alias itself, not a narrower `Dict[ButtonDataKey, ...]`.

title: Phase 5b code review findings: tag-filter wizard defects and recommendations
content:
CODE REVIEW of Phase 5b tag-filter wizard (2026-07-07, review-only, no edits). **Verdict: mergeable — no critical (🔴) or important (🟡) issues.** All findings are recommendations (🔵) or nitpicks (⚪). Core pagination logic, user-scoping, and exception handling were verified correct.

## Actionable bug (🔵 recommendation, 2-line fix)
**TagFilter back button drops page offset** — `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py:2264-2271`. The "back" button in `_handleConfigAction_TagFilter` hardcodes `ButtonDataKey.Page: 0`, but the entry-point buttons (lines 1813-1818 "Фильтр: #tag (изменить)" and 1840-1845 "Фильтр по тегу") carry the actual current offset. So a user on page 5 of a tag-filtered list who opens the tag picker then clicks "Назад" lands on page 0, losing their scroll position. Fix: read `offset = int(data.get(ButtonDataKey.Page, 0) or 0)` (already present in payload) and forward it in `backPayload`.

## Non-obvious gotcha (🔵 recommendation)
**Tag lowercasing assumption is imprecise** — `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:582-584` docstring claims "Tags are stored lowercased by `add_memory`". This is only TRUE for the LLM-tool wrapper `UserDataHandler._llmToolAddMemory` (`user_data.py:557`, does `[t.lower() for t in ...]`). The repo method `UserMemoriesRepository.addMemory` does NOT lowercase, nor does `updateMemory(tags=...)`. Consequence: `getDistinctTags` could return BOTH "Work" and "work" as distinct entries if any non-LLM insertion path persists mixed-case tags (migration backfill, future tag-editing UI, direct repo calls in tests). The `searchMemories` tag filter is a set-intersection — case-sensitive — so picking "Work" wouldn't match "work"-tagged memories. Recommendation: either soften the docstring OR lowercase defensively in `getDistinctTags` (`distinctTags.add(tag.lower())`).

## Design limitations (🔵, accepted v1 tradeoffs)
1. **Tag picker has no button-count cap** — `_handleConfigAction_TagFilter:2292-2306` renders one row per distinct tag with no pagination. A user with 30+ tags produces a very tall inline keyboard. The memory list is capped at `KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE = 8`; the tag picker has no equivalent. Mitigation needed if tag universe grows.
2. **Tag button labels not truncated** — `f"#{tag}"` (line 2296) and `f"Фильтр: #{tag} (изменить)"` (line 1811) render raw tags. Memory previews go through `_truncateForButton` (line 2187); tags do not. Reuse it.
3. **Performance: re-fetches all 200 rows per page nav** — under tag filter, each Next/Prev re-runs `searchMemories(limit=200, offset=0)` then slices in Python. Acceptable for admin-only wizard but worth a follow-up.

## Test gaps (🔵 — regression risk)
In `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py:391-454`, the `getDistinctTags` defensive paths are NOT tested:
- **Malformed JSON** in `tags` column (the `except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError)` branch ~line 617). Insert `tags='not-json'` via raw SQL, assert it's skipped.
- **NULL `tags` column** (the `if not rawTags: continue` guard ~line 613). Insert `tags=NULL`, assert skipped.

In `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data.py`:
- `test_tagFilterPersistsAcrossPagination` (line 2626) asserts NextPage carries tag but does NOT assert PrevPage does (PrevPage also carries it — symmetric assertion missing).
- The v1 limitation "MemorySelected back button drops the tag" has no regression test. Add one asserting the MemorySelected payload does NOT carry `ButtonDataKey.Tag` (locks the contract).

## sqlToTypedDict bypass — confirmed justified
`getDistinctTags` accesses `row["tags"]` / `row.keys()` directly, bypassing `sqlToTypedDict`. Verified this is correct: `sqlToTypedDict` requires ALL required keys of the TypedDict (UserMemoryDict has many), so calling it on a `SELECT tags FROM ...` result would `KeyError`. The direct-access pattern is portable for both sqlite3.Row and dict row types.

## Confirmed clean
- **Dangling references:** grep confirms `TagFilter`/`ButtonDataKey.Tag` used only in enums.py, user_data.py, wizard tests, plan doc. No stray consumers.
- **User-scoping airtight:** every read path (`getDistinctTags`, `searchMemories`, wizard handlers) uses `userId = user.id` from callback sender, never from payload. SQL parameterised on `(chatId, userId)`.
- **hasNext math correct** for all boundary cases including the 200-cap truncation.
- **AGENTS.md conventions:** camelCase, docstrings w/ Args/Returns, type hints, no `Any`, StrEnum, UPPER_CASE constant — all compliant.

title: GOTCHA: user_memories.tags column is NOT NULL — use empty string in tests, not NULL
content:
Discovered when writing defensive tests for `getDistinctTags` (Phase 5b Gate 1 fix, 2026-07-07).

**Symptom:** Setting a row's `tags` column to `NULL` via raw SQL in a test fails immediately:
```
sqlite3.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: user_memories.tags
```

**Root cause:** The `user_memories.tags` column is declared `TEXT NOT NULL` in the schema (migration). NULL can never legitimately occur at runtime — every insert path (`addMemory`, `updateMemory`, `_llmToolAddMemory`) supplies at least `[]`.

**Fix/implication for tests:** To exercise the `if not rawTags: continue` defensive guard in `getDistinctTags` (~line 613 of `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`), use an empty string `''` instead of NULL. Empty string is falsy, so the guard skips it — same defensive path. The guard handles both NULL (defensive, never occurs) and `''` (realistic, could occur via a bad backfill).

**Raw SQL convention in `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py`:** Tests that need to bypass the repository use:
```python
sqlProvider = await testDatabase.manager.getProvider(chatId=CHAT_ID, readonly=False)
await sqlProvider.execute("UPDATE user_memories SET tags = :tags WHERE memory_id = :mid", {"tags": "not-json", "mid": memoryId})
```
i.e. `manager.getProvider(chatId=…, readonly=False)` + `execute(rawSqlString, paramsDict)` — NOT wrapped in `ParametrizedQuery`. This matches the existing convention in the file (e.g. `test_deleteMemoriesByQuery_olderThanDays`). The task spec suggested `ParametrizedQuery` but explicitly said "check how other tests in the file do raw SQL" — the answer is the raw-string pattern.

title: deleteMemoriesByQuery is dead code — zero production callers after ClearChatData removal
content:
Found in Gate 2 cross-cutting review of user-memories (2026-07-07, branch `user-memory-v2`).

**`UserMemoriesRepository.deleteMemoriesByQuery`** (`internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:383–446`, ~64 LOC) has ZERO production callers. Grep across `internal/bot/` confirms no matches. It is exercised only by 5 tests in `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py`.

**Root cause:** The method was created to serve the `/knowledge_config` wizard's `ClearChatData` action. In Phase 5a, `ClearChatData` was REMOVED entirely (per memory `8dde0248`: "research said repoint to deleteMemoriesByQuery; actual: REMOVED entirely") rather than repointed. This orphaned the method.

**Why the `delete_memory` LLM tool doesn't use it:** The by-query tool path (user_data.py:644–659) calls `searchMemories` + unrestricted `deleteMemory` (by-id) in a loop — because by-query delete needs to reach PERMANENT memories (an explicit, LLM-reviewed action), whereas `deleteMemoriesByQuery` is permanent-guarded (`AND permanent = 0`). The two serve different purposes.

**Impact:** The method is listed in the canonical doc (`user-memories.md:92`) and module docstring (`user_memories.py:10`) as a live repo method, creating a false impression of a supported API surface. A future contributor might call it expecting production-tested behavior, or waste time keeping it in sync with schema changes.

**Recommendation:** Remove `deleteMemoriesByQuery` + its 5 tests (YAGNI — cleanest option). Alternatively, if retaining for potential future bulk-ephemeral cleanup, add a docstring note "No production callers as of Phase 5a" and drop from canonical doc's method list.

title: Circular import: internal/database/models.py must not import from internal.bot.models
content:
Durable architectural constraint discovered in commit 85aa945 ("Massive memories-feature refactoring").

The refactoring moved `UserMemoryDict` from `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py` into `internal/database/models.py` (correcting the convention deviation flagged in memories 3dc92f88/7d2089a7) AND retyped its `type` field from `str` to `MemoryType`. `MemoryType` lives in `internal/bot/models/memory_type.py`. The new import at `internal/database/models.py:12`:

```python
from internal.bot.models.memory_type import MemoryType
```

creates a HARD circular import that breaks the ENTIRE app (not just tests):

  internal.database.__init__ → internal.database.database
  → internal.database.repositories (imports UserMemoryDict from ..models)
  → internal.database.models (now needs MemoryType from internal.bot.models)
  → internal.bot.models.__init__ → .command_handlers → .ensured_message
  → `from internal.database import Database`
  → ImportError: cannot import name 'Database' from partially initialized module

This is distinct from the circular import documented in memory a15ce096 (which is about `internal/bot/models/__init__.py` re-exporting `MessageType` via a 3-dot relative import — a DIFFERENT cycle that was successfully avoided there).

LESSON: `internal/database/models.py` is imported very early in the `internal.database` package init, before `internal.database.Database` is fully defined. ANY import it pulls in from `internal.bot.models.*` risks the same cycle (because `internal/bot/models/` transitively imports back into `internal.database` via `ensured_message` / `command_handlers`). When a database-row TypedDict needs a type that lives in `internal.bot.models`, either: keep that field typed as `str` (the old, working approach), or move the shared type to a neutral location (`internal/models/` or `lib/`) that neither package init depends on. Do NOT import across the database↔bot.models boundary from `database/models.py`.

This P0 bug currently blocks app startup and all test collection in commit 85aa945.

title: Memories-feature architecture after 85aa945 refactoring (supersedes old injection path)
content:
SUPERSEDES memory 08b23660 (which documented the Phase 4b injection path via `BaseBotHandler._buildMemoriesBlock` + `_injectMemoriesBlock`). Commit 85aa945 ("Massive memories-feature refactoring", 25 files, +850/−1360, net −510 LOC) reorganizes the user-memories feature that shipped 2026-07-07. The new architecture:

1. **Memory injection centralized.** The scattered `_buildMemoriesBlock`/`_injectMemoriesBlock`/`_safeEmbedQuery`/`_formatMemoryLine` calls (previously in `base.py` + 3 sites in `llm_messages.py`) are DELETED. Injection now happens in ONE place: new `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories()` at message-arrival time. Memories are PERSISTED into the chat message's `metadata` JSON so they ride along in thread context. `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage(..., injectMemories: bool)` (new keyword-only param) reads them back. Field/method rename: `userData`→`userMemories`, `setUserData`→`setUserMemories`.

2. **Embedding logic consolidated into LLMService.** `internal/bot/common/memory_embedding_utils.py` DELETED wholesale (the `embedAndSaveMemory` helper). `_resolveEmbeddingModel`/`_floatsToBytes` removed from `UserDataHandler`. New `LLMService.generateEmbedding(text, chatId, chatSettings) -> Optional[Tuple[modelName, List[float]]]` centralizes model resolution + rate-limiting. Callers no longer touch float↔bytes serialization. NOTE: `generateEmbedding` currently has a "TODO write docstring" placeholder (AGENTS.md violation).

3. **Repository API overhaul (`user_memories.py`).** Embeddings now carried as `List[float]` + an `embeddingModel: str` name (was `bytes` + `dimensions`). `addMemory`: new required `embedding`/`embeddingModel`/`source` params, `source` retyped `str`→`UserMemorySource` (new StrEnum), `threadId` moved to keyword-only, embeds during add. `searchMemories`: `queryEmbedding` bytes→floats, `dimensions`→`embeddingModel`. `saveMemoryEmbedding`: `model`→`embeddingModel`, float input. `deleteMemoriesByQuery` REMOVED (resolves dead-code memory cdd9f18c; 4 covering tests deleted). Tag filtering moved from Python post-filter to SQL `LIKE`, centralized in new `_normalizeTags()` (lowercase/dedupe/strip-quotes). `cleanupObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` return type changed `int`→`None` and lost its top-level try/except.

4. **vec0 table gains `model` partition-key column.** `vec_user_memories_{dim}` now created with a `model` TEXT partition key; semantic search filters by model name. WARNING: only the lazy-create path was updated — migration_020 was NOT amended, so pre-existing vec0 tables lack the column (see separate bug memory).

5. **Cache API replaced.** `CacheService.getChatUserData`/`setChatUserData`/`unsetChatUserData`/`clearChatUserData` (old key-value `userData` store) DELETED. Replaced by `getChatUserPermanentMemories`/`invalidateChatUserPermanentMemories`. Cache dict key `data` → `permanentMemories: Dict[int, list[SingleMemoryDict]]`.

6. **Model extraction.** `MetadataDict`/`CondensingDict` moved `ensured_message.py`→new `message_metadata.py` (`MetadataDict` gains a `memories` field). New `SingleMemoryDict`, `UserMemoriesDict`, `convertDBMemoryToSingleMemoryDict`. `UserMemorySource` StrEnum. `UserMemoryDict` moved repo→`internal/database/models.py`, `type` retyped `str`→`MemoryType` (this is what caused the P0 circular import — see separate memory). `numpy` added as a dependency (vector norm check).

BREAKING public-ish API changes: addMemory/searchMemories/saveMemoryEmbedding signatures, CacheService.getChatUserData* removed, EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage new required injectMemories, userData→userMemories.

title: user_memories tags serialization VERIFIED: raw list safe end-to-end, no json.dumps needed
content:
Verification (2026-07-09) of the user_memories `tags` field round-trip. After the refactoring, `UserMemoriesRepository.addMemory`/`updateMemory` bind `_normalizeTags(tags)` (a Python `list`) directly as the TEXT column value instead of `json.dumps(tags)`. This was flagged as a potential bug (sqlite3 rejects list params for TEXT) but is CORRECT as-is — no `json.dumps` wrapper needed at the binding site.

This confirms the general provider auto-conversion pattern documented in memories 0fe05e3a / 31fe7c24 applies to the user_memories tags case specifically, on BOTH paths:

**Write path:** `SQLite3Provider._execute` (internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py:328) and `batchExecute` (:346) wrap params with `utils.convertContainerElementsToSQLite(query.params)`, which maps every dict value through `convertToSQLite`. `convertToSQLite` (providers/utils.py:53) matches `isinstance(data, (dict, list, tuple, Mapping, Sequence))` → `libUtils.jsonDumps(data)`. `upsert` routes through `execute()` → same path. So a raw `list` is serialized to a JSON string before binding. (Note: `str` and `bool` are matched by earlier isinstance branches, so they don't accidentally hit the Sequence branch.)

**Read path (list[str] specifically — not previously documented):** `sqlToCustomType` (internal/database/utils.py) for a `tags: list[str]` field: data is a JSON string; `_checkType` fails (str isn't list); skips bool/int/float/TypedDict branches; hits `expectedType in CONTAINER_TYPES` (list is in LIST_LIKE_TYPES ⊂ CONTAINER_TYPES) → `data = json.loads(data)`; falls through to the `SEQUENCE_LIKE_TYPES` branch which converts each item to `str`. So the JSON TEXT is parsed back to `list[str]`.

Takeaway for future repo work: any repo passing `list`/`dict`/`Sequence` values directly in SQL params gets automatic JSON ↔ Python round-tripping through the provider layer — do NOT manually `json.dumps()` at binding sites, and do NOT manually `json.loads()` on read for container-typed TypedDict fields.

title: Refactored UserMemoriesRepository API signatures (commit 85aa945 refactor)
content:
The "Massive memories-feature refactoring" (commit 85aa945, branch `user-memory-v2`) changed these `UserMemoriesRepository` (`internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`) method signatures. Tests and callers must match:

title: 4 open production bugs in user_memories.py (found during test-fix, NOT fixed)
content:
Found 2026-07-09 while fixing test files for the refactoring (branch `user-memory-v2`, commit 85aa945). These are production bugs where the implementation does NOT match its own docstring. Tests encode the correct (docstring) contracts and correctly FAIL. DO NOT weaken these tests to mask the bugs. NOT fixed because production was out of scope for that task.

1. **Missing `await` at `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:1081`** (`_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`): `if not sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported():` calls an ASYNC method WITHOUT `await`. The guard evaluates a coroutine object's truthiness (always truthy → `not` is falsy → the `return False` is dead code), and emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'SQLite3Provider.isVectorSearchSupported' was never awaited`. Every other call site (lines ~784, ~1201) correctly uses `await`. FIX: add `await`.

2. **`deleteMemory` (~307-351) return contract broken**: docstring promises "True if a row was deleted, False if no row matched", but impl always returns `True` on success — no existence/row-count check. Re-deleting a non-existent row returns `True`. The sibling `updateMemory` correctly does an existence pre-check; `deleteMemory` lacks it. FIX: add a pre-check (SELECT before DELETE) like `updateMemory` does.

3. **`deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` (~1320-1390) is incomplete**: typed `-> None`, docstring promises "Returns: the count of reset rows. Never raises." Body neither counts reset rows NOR resets the `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` columns on `user_memories` to NULL — it only deletes vec0 rows. FIX: return the count and reset provenance columns (the test at `test_deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` documents expected behavior).

4. **`deleteMemoryEmbedding` (~1154-1247) bool return broken**: docstring promises "False when tables existed but the memory_id was not found in any of them", but impl returns `True` unconditionally at ~line 1239. The companion SELECTs check existence but never drive the return value. FIX: track whether a DELETE actually ran and return False otherwise.

Affected tests (all in `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py`): `test_deleteMemory`, `test_deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings`, `test_deleteMemoryEmbedding_returnsFalseWhenNoMatch`.

title: isVectorSearchSupported async — calling without await makes guards dead code
content:
Production bug pattern (fixed 2026-07-09, branch `user-memory-v2`, `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`):

`BaseSQLProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()` (and other provider methods like `getProvider`) are `async def`. Calling them WITHOUT `await` in a guard, e.g. `if not sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported():`, evaluates a coroutine object's truthiness. A coroutine is ALWAYS truthy, so `not <coroutine>` is ALWAYS `False` — the guard branch becomes unreachable dead code. It also emits `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '...isVectorSearchSupported' was never awaited`.

This bit `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding` (the vector-support guard silently never short-circuited). Every OTHER call site in the same file correctly uses `await sqlProvider.isVectorSearchSupported()`. Fix was simply adding `await`.

GENERAL RULE: any provider method accessed as `sqlProvider.<asyncMethod>()` must be awaited. When writing or reviewing a guard around `isVectorSearchSupported()` / `getProvider()` / similar, check for `await`. The test-mocking variant of this gotcha (MagicMock returns a plain bool that can't be awaited → `TypeError: 'bool' object can't be awaited`) is the mirror image and was recorded separately.

Also fixed in the same pass: `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`'s docstring had drifted — it claimed `Returns: None` and `Raises: Re-raised after logging`, but the actual signature is `-> bool` and the code catches exceptions and `return False` (never re-raises). `saveMemoryEmbedding` checks BOTH the bool return (`if not await self._upsertVecMemoryEmbedding(...): return False`) and wraps in try/except, so it tolerates either failure mode.

title: user_memories delete/embedding return contracts fixed (refactoring regressions)
content:
Four return-contract bugs in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`, introduced by the "massive memories-feature refactoring" (commit 85aa945) and FIXED 2026-07-09 (branch `user-memory-v2`). The tests in `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py` encode the correct (docstring) contracts and correctly FAILED before the fix — do not weaken them. All 4 are now fixed and verified; the repo test file is fully green (34 tests).

1. `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`: missing `await` on `isVectorSearchSupported()` (see separate memory).

2. `deleteMemory` (was ~307-351): docstring promises "True if a row was deleted, False if no row matched", but impl always returned True on success. FIX: added an existence pre-check (`SELECT 1 FROM user_memories WHERE chat_id/user_id/memory_id`) before the DELETE — mirrors the sibling `updateMemory` which already does an existence pre-check. Re-deleting a non-existent memoryId now correctly returns False. Never-raise try/except wrapping preserved (returns False on exception).

3. `deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` (was ~1320-1390): incomplete — typed `-> None`, never counted/reset rows. FIX: restored `-> int`; added `SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt` (then `row["cnt"]`, matching `bayes_storage.py`'s `as vocab_size` pattern) before cleanup; added the missing `UPDATE user_memories SET embedding_model=NULL, embedding_dimensions=NULL`; restored never-raise try/except (returns 0). See separate memory for why the column reset is the linchpin.

4. `deleteMemoryEmbedding` (was ~1154-1247): docstring promises "False when tables existed but memory_id not found", but impl returned True unconditionally. FIX: introduced a `deletedAny` flag initialized False, set True ONLY inside the two successful DELETE branches (metadata-keyed DELETE succeeds, or rowid-fallback DELETE actually runs). Preserved "no vec0 table → True" no-op-success semantics via early returns.

Affected/regression tests (all pass post-fix): `test_deleteMemory`, `test_deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings`, `test_deleteMemoryEmbedding_returnsFalseWhenNoMatch`.

title: deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings ↔ getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings column-reset contract (model-drift linchpin)
content:
Data-flow / architecture contract for the memory-embedding regen cron in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`.

The regen cron's stale-detection is PROVENANCE-COLUMN based, not vec0-row based. `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings(chatId, modelName, dimensions, limit)` surfaces rows where `embedding_model IS NULL OR embedding_model != :modelName OR embedding_dimensions IS NULL OR embedding_dimensions != :dimensions`. Therefore, for the regen loop to pick up stale rows, the `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` columns on `user_memories` MUST be NULLed out — the mere absence of a vec0 row is NOT enough.

`deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel, currentDimensions) -> int` is the MODEL-DRIFT cleanup step that runs FIRST in the regen sequence. It MUST do BOTH:
  (a) delete the stale vec0 rows from `vec_user_memories_{N}` tables, AND
  (b) `UPDATE user_memories SET embedding_model=NULL, embedding_dimensions=NULL WHERE <stale predicate>`.

If (b) is skipped (this was the refactoring bug), `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` never re-surfaces the stale rows → the regen cron's stale-detection loop is SILENTLY BROKEN (rows stay with old-model provenance forever, never re-embedded). This is the model-drift complement to the content-drift path: `updateMemory` nulling those columns on content edits (recorded in the "content edits invalidate embeddings" memory) is the SAME invariant.

Stale predicate (shared by the COUNT and the UPDATE so they stay in lockstep):
`chat_id = :chatId AND embedding_model IS NOT NULL AND (embedding_model != :currentModel OR embedding_dimensions != :currentDimensions)`
— guarded by `embedding_model IS NOT NULL` so never-embedded rows (already NULL) aren't touched (they're surfaced by getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings already).

CONVENTION: when `currentDimensions` is Optional (dim-less embedding models), branch explicitly on `currentDimensions is None` to build the WHERE string rather than relying on SQL three-valued `col != :dim` (where `:dim=None` → NULL → falsy). This mirrors the `chat_embeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` precedent and avoids subtle NULL-comparison bugs across SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL. The COUNT and UPDATE share ONE predicate string.

Implementation note: COUNT uses `SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt` → `row["cnt"]` (int cast), same shape as `bayes_storage.py`'s `as vocab_size`.

title: Test mocking gotcha: mock generateEmbedding/resolveModel directly, not getLLMManager, after 85aa945 refactoring
content:
After the memories-feature refactoring (commit 85aa945), testing code that resolves embedding models has a non-obvious trap.

**The problem:** The old test helper pattern was `_stubEmbeddingModel(handler, model)` which set `handler.llmService.getLLMManager = Mock(return_value=Mock(getModel=Mock(return_value=mockModel)))`. This worked when production code called `self.llmService.getLLMManager().getModel(name)` directly. But the refactored code now calls `self.llmService.resolveModel(ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL, chatSettings=..., defaultKey=...)`, which internally calls `chatSettings[key].toModel()`, which calls the MODULE-LEVEL `getLLMManager()` function in `chat_settings.py` (line 25). That module-level function has its own `_llmManager` cache (set once, never reset by conftest's `LLMService._instance = None` fixture). So the instance-level mock on `handler.llmService.getLLMManager` is invisible to the `toModel()` path.

**The fix:** Mock `handler.llmService.generateEmbedding` and/or `handler.llmService.resolveModel` directly at the `handler.llmService` attribute level. Example:

```python
def _stubGenerateEmbedding(handler, *, result=None):
    mock = AsyncMock(return_value=result)
    handler.llmService.generateEmbedding = mock  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return mock
```

Pass `result=("test-embed-model", [0.1, 0.2, 0.3])` for a successful embedding (returns `Tuple[modelName, floats]`), or `result=None` for the model-not-found / embedding-disabled case.

**Also:** `patch("internal.bot.common.handlers.user_data.embedAndSaveMemory", ...)` will raise `AttributeError` at test runtime because `embedAndSaveMemory` is no longer imported into `user_data.py` (only docstring/comment references remain at lines 820, 917). Remove all such patches.

**addMemory test seed calls:** After the refactoring, `db.userMemories.addMemory(...)` requires three new params: `source` (a `UserMemorySource` enum), `embedding` (Optional[List[float]]), `embeddingModel` (Optional[str]). For test seeding, add `source=UserMemorySource.CHAT, embedding=None, embeddingModel=None`.

**Rendering logic location:** The `BaseBotHandler._formatMemoriesBlock` staticmethod was removed, but equivalent rendering logic survives as module-level function `_formatMemoriesBlockRaw(permanent, ephemeral)` at `user_data.py:158`. Import as `from internal.bot.common.handlers.user_data import _formatMemoriesBlockRaw`. Tests that previously called `BaseBotHandler._formatMemoriesBlock` can be repointed here.

**The deleted methods `_buildMemoriesBlock`/`_injectMemoriesBlock`** are GONE entirely — not on BaseBotHandler, not on MessagePreprocessorHandler. They were replaced by `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories(ensuredMessage)` which has a completely different API (takes EnsuredMessage, returns None, sets `userMemories`). Old tests for these cannot be trivially ported.

title: Coverage gap: MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories() has zero test coverage after 85aa945 refactoring
content:
The memories-feature refactoring (commit 85aa945) centralized memory injection into `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories(ensuredMessage)` — the method that fetches permanent + ephemeral/search memories and sets `ensuredMessage.userMemories` at message-arrival time.

However, `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_preprocessor.py` does NOT test `injectMemories()`. That file only covers:
- The embedding-dispatch hook (`embedAndSaveMessage` background task gating)
- The chat-member handler (`leftChatMemberHandler`)

The memory-injection decision logic that was previously tested via `TestBuildMemoriesBlock` / `TestFormatMemoriesBlock` / `TestInjectMemoriesBlock` in `test_base.py` (which tested `_buildMemoriesBlock(chatId, userId, threadId, text, chatSettings) -> str`) has NO direct replacement coverage. title: _runMemoryEmbeddingRegen post-refactoring: resolveModel ValueError uncaught, supportsEmbedding check removed, stale docstrings
content:
After the memories-feature refactoring (commit 85aa945), `UserDataHandler._runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` has three production code issues discovered during test fixing on 2026-07-09:

**1. `resolveModel` ValueError propagates uncaught (docstring/code discrepancy)**
The method calls `self.llmService.resolveModel(ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL, chatSettings=..., defaultKey=...)` at ~line 867-869 WITHOUT a local try/except. When the model is empty or unknown, `ChatSettingsValue.toModel()` raises `ValueError` (because `getLLMManager().getModel("")` returns `None`). The exception propagates out of `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen`. It IS caught by the `_dtCronJob` wrapper (`except Exception: logger.exception(...)`), so production is safe — but the method's own docstring (step 4) says it should "bail" (graceful return), not raise. Tests that call `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` directly (not via `_dtCronJob`) must use `pytest.raises(ValueError)` and assert cleanup/fetch were not reached (they aren't, since the ValueError fires before them).

**2. `supportsEmbedding` check removed from the regen path**
The refactored production code no longer checks `model.supportsEmbedding` before proceeding to cleanup/stale-detection/re-embed. The check effectively moved INTO `LLMService.generateEmbedding`'s internal try/except — if `embeddingModel.generateEmbeddings(text)` fails (model doesn't support it), `generateEmbedding` catches the exception and returns `None`, and the re-embed loop's `if memoryEmbedding is not None:` guard skips that memory. The step-4 docstring still says "bail when... not embedding-capable" but the code doesn't implement this check anymore. The test `test_skipsWhenModelLacksEmbeddingSupport` had to be removed because the behavior it tested no longer exists.

**3. Stale docstrings**
- Step-7 docstring (~line 820-821) still says "re-embedded via `embedAndSaveMemory`" but the code now calls `self.llmService.generateEmbedding()` + `self.db.userMemories.saveMemoryEmbedding()` directly.
- Step-4 docstring says "bail when empty, unknown, or not embedding-capable" but (as noted above) the code raises ValueError on empty/unknown and doesn't check embedding-capable at all.

**Context for testing:** The new call chain in the re-embed loop is:
```python
memoryEmbedding = await self.llmService.generateEmbedding(memory["content"], chatId=chatId, chatSettings=chatSettings)
if memoryEmbedding is not None:
    if await self.db.userMemories.saveMemoryEmbedding(chatId=chatId, userId=memory["user_id"], memoryId=memory["memory_id"], embedding=memoryEmbedding[1], embeddingModel=memoryEmbedding[0]):
        embedded += 1
```
`generateEmbedding` returns `Optional[Tuple[str, List[float]]]` — `None` on failure, `(modelName, embeddingVector)` on success. The first element is passed to `saveMemoryEmbedding` as `embeddingModel`, the second as `embedding`.

title: Memory injection moved from handler-level to preprocessor-time (supersedes 08b23860)
content:
SUPERSEDES memory 08b23860 (Phase 4b, 2026-07-07) which documented that the `<user-memories>` system-message block via `BaseBotHandler._buildMemoriesBlock` + `_injectMemoriesBlock` was the SOLE active memory-injection path.

As of 2026-07-09, that handler-level injection path was REMOVED ENTIRELY in a later refactoring. The methods `_buildMemoriesBlock` and `_injectMemoriesBlock` no longer exist on `BaseBotHandler` (confirmed by grep; `test_base.py` documents their removal, and the `TestBuildMemoriesBlock`/`TestInjectMemoriesBlock` classes were deleted).

**New architecture:**
- Memory injection now happens at PREPROCESSOR arrival time: `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories(ensuredMessage)` runs in `newMessageHandler` (called unconditionally, message_preprocessor.py line ~162).
- `injectMemories` fetches memories via `self.cache.getChatUserPermanentMemories(...)` and attaches them to the `EnsuredMessage` via `ensuredMessage.setUserMemories(...)`.
- Memories then travel PER-MESSAGE as structured `userMemories` data, rendered by `formatForLLM` as a JSON field — NOT as a `<user-memories>` XML block injected into the system message at handler time.
- At handler time (`handleMention`, `handleRandomMessage`, `handleReply`), the system message is built purely from `CHAT_PROMPT + CHAT_PROMPT_SUFFIX`. No memory block is injected there.
- Historical messages load their memories via `fromDBChatMessage(..., injectMemories=injectMemories)`.

**Gotcha for tests:** `injectMemories` reads `chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.MEMORY_INJECTION_ENABLED]` directly (message_preprocessor.py line ~85) BEFORE any guard. Any test chat-settings helper that flows through `newMessageHandler` MUST include `MEMORY_INJECTION_ENABLED` (set to `"false"` to short-circuit; with it false, `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE` is never read). This caused 6 `KeyError: MEMORY_INJECTION_ENABLED` failures in test_message_preprocessor.py when the `_defaultChatSettings()` helper omitted it.

**Coverage note:** The `[FINDING]` in `test_base.py` flags that `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories` (the new injection path) has NO dedicated test coverage as of 2026-07-09. The old handler-level injection tests were deleted (matching the method removal), but replacement preprocessor-level injectMemories tests have not yet been written.

Verified: `make test` = 3031 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failures (2026-07-09).

title: BUG: _runRefinement backward-compat placeholder aliases NOT actually passed (stale comment)
content:
[FINDING / latent production bug — 2026-07-09]

In `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`, the comment block at lines ~1247-1252 claims that `existingUserData` / `existingSummary` are passed to `userPromptTemplate.format(...)` as backward-compat aliases so that stale per-chat overrides of `MEMORY_REFINE_USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` (still referencing the OLD placeholders `{existingUserData}`/`{existingSummary}`) keep formatting without raising KeyError.

BUT the actual `.format()` call (lines ~1253-1256) ONLY passes `messages` and `existingMemories`:
```python
userPrompt = userPromptTemplate.format(
    messages=rendered,
    existingMemories=existingMemoriesText,
)
```

So a deployed per-chat override whose `MEMORY_REFINE_USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` still references `{existingUserData}` or `{existingSummary}` WILL raise `KeyError` at refinement time. The background refinement run is try/except-wrapped further out so it won't crash the bot, but that user's memory will silently stop refining.

This relates to memory d845a2c4 (Phase 4a) which documented the INTENT to keep these backward-compat aliases — that intent was never actually implemented in the `.format()` call.

**Fix options** (production code — was out of scope for the test-only session that found this):
1. Make the comment true: add `existingUserData=existingMemoriesText, existingSummary=existingMemoriesText` to the `.format()` call, OR
2. Drop the stale comment (acknowledge backward-compat was deliberately dropped).

Flagged to the user on 2026-07-09; not yet resolved.

title: deleteMemory repo method cascades to deleteMemoryEmbedding internally (embedding cleanup is repo-level)
content:
Architecture detail (2026-07-09): The `UserMemoriesRepository.deleteMemory` method (internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py, line ~307) internally cascades to embedding cleanup — it calls `await self.deleteMemoryEmbedding(chatId, userId, memoryId, vecOnly=True)` at line ~366.

**Consequence for handlers and tests:** The handler `_llmToolDeleteMemory` (user_data.py) by-id path only calls `db.userMemories.deleteMemory(chatId, userId, memory_id)` — it does NOT separately call `deleteMemoryEmbedding`. The embedding cleanup is owned by the repo method, not the handler. So deleting a memory WITHOUT deleting its vec0 embedding does NOT leave orphaned vectors — the cascade handles it.

**Test gotcha:** In tests that mock the repo (e.g. `_mockUserMemories` replaces the entire `handler.db.userMemories` with a bare `Mock`), `deleteMemory` becomes an `AsyncMock` that does NOT cascade. So asserting `mockRepo.deleteMemoryEmbedding.assert_awaited_once()` at the handler level is WRONG — the cascade lives inside the real (mocked-away) repo method. The correct handler-level assertion is `mockRepo.deleteMemory.assert_awaited_once_with(chatId, userId, memoryId)`. The cascade itself is covered at the repo level in tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py.

This is NOT a production bug — the production code correctly delegates embedding cleanup to the repo.

title: _runRefinement template: {existingUserData}/{existingSummary} placeholders intentionally removed
content:
The "Massive memories-feature refactoring" (commit 85aa945) intentionally removed the `{existingUserData}` and `{existingSummary}` placeholders from the memory-refinement template (`MEMO_REFINE_*`) format call in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` `_runRefinement`. Only `{existingMemories}` and `{messages}` are now passed to `userPromptTemplate.format(...)`.

**Operational gotcha:** A deployed per-chat override of `MEMO_REFINE_*` templates that still references the old `{existingUserData}` or `{existingSummary}` placeholders will raise `KeyError` inside `_runRefinement`. This is caught by the method's outer `try/except`, so it fails silently — refinement simply stops for that user with no crash. Operators upgrading past this refactoring should audit any custom `MEMO_REFINE_*` overrides and migrate them to use `{existingMemories}`.

The backward-compat aliases were deliberately NOT restored (the refactoring intentionally consolidated memory context into the single `{existingMemories}` placeholder). An inline comment in the code now documents this.

title: Tags filter in searchMemories now SQL LIKE (supersedes Python set-intersection post-filter)
content:
CORRECTION to memory 0713dca6 (2026-07-07), which documented `searchMemories` tags filtering as a **Python set-intersection post-filter running AFTER SQL `LIMIT ... OFFSET ...`** (`results = [r for r in results if requestedTags & set(r.get("tags") or [])]`), and the resulting pagination-interaction bug.

As of the memories refactoring (commit 85aa945, 2026-07-09), the tags filter was changed BACK to **SQL `LIKE`** in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`:
- `_filterOnlySearchMemories` (~lines 716-725) builds `tags LIKE :tagsN` clauses.
- `_semanticSearchMemories` (~lines 907-917) also uses `tags LIKE`.

Tags are now stored via provider auto-serialization (list → JSON TEXT). The matching is SQL `LIKE` (`%tag%`-style), not exact Python set-intersection.

**Impact on the pagination gotcha (0713dca6):** Because `LIKE` runs in the SQL `WHERE` clause (before `LIMIT/OFFSET`), the offset-interaction bug that 0713dca6 documented should now be RESOLVED at the repository level. However, 0713dca6's wizard-level workaround in `_renderMemoryList` (fetch a generous batch at offset 0, paginate in Python when a tag filter is active) was deliberately left in place. That workaround is now likely unnecessary/harmless and should be audited — the next person touching the wizard should verify whether the Python-side pagination can be dropped now that tags filtering is SQL-level.

**Tags serialization caveat:** memory f30a9bc2 flagged "tags serialization likely broken" because `addMemory` passes a raw list to a TEXT column. The refactoring relies on provider auto-serialization to convert the list to JSON TEXT. Verify this actually works end-to-end if debugging tag search.

title: searchMemories API: callers pass List[float] not bytes; embeddingModel selects vec0 table (serialisation is internal)
content:
The `UserMemoriesRepository` search API contract (internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py), finalised during the user-memories refactoring (2026-07-09):

**`searchMemories(chatId, userId, queryEmbedding: Optional[List[float]]=None, *, ..., embeddingModel: Optional[str], ...)`** — the public entry point. Two modes, selected by:
- Filter-only mode: `queryEmbedding is None OR embeddingModel is None` → plain SQL scan of `user_memories` with optional threadId/type/tags/permanent filters.
- Semantic mode: both `queryEmbedding` (a non-empty `List[float]`) AND `embeddingModel` set → native vec0 search over `vec_user_memories_{dim}`, JOIN back to `user_memories` by `memory_id`; `score = 1.0 - distance`.

**`_semanticSearchMemories(..., queryEmbedding: List[float], *, ..., embeddingModel: str, ...)`** — the internal semantic implementation. Takes `List[float]` directly.

**KEY DESIGN DECISION (diverges from chat_search.py precedent):** Callers pass `List[float]`, NOT pre-serialised float32 bytes. The float32 BLOB serialisation (`array.array("f", floats).tobytes()`) happens INSIDE the repo (`_semanticSearchMemories` / `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`), not at call sites. This is the opposite of the chat_history/embeddings path where `array.array("f", vec).tobytes()` is done by callers/repositories explicitly. The `embeddingModel` name selects which model-partitioned vec0 table to search (vec0 is partitioned by dimension `vec_user_memories_{dim}`); there is NO `dimensions` parameter — the dimension is derived from the embedding list length / tracked via `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` provenance columns on the `user_memories` row itself.

NOTE: An earlier version of this API took `queryEmbedding: bytes` (pre-serialised) plus a `dimensions` int param; that was refactored away. Docstrings referencing `bytes`/`dimensions` were stale and fixed in this session. The `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings`/`deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` methods at the bottom of the file legitimately have a real `dimensions`/`currentDimensions` parameter (model-drift regeneration) — those are NOT stale.

title: make lint pipeline: flake8 → isort → import-main check → pyright (all Python-only, no markdown linter)
content:
`make lint` runs FOUR commands in the Makefile `lint` target (order matters):

1. `flake8 .` — Python parser; only processes `.py`/`.pyi`.
2. `isort --check-only --diff .` — sorts imports in Python files only.
3. **`import main` circular-import check** (added 2026-07-09 after the `85aa945` refactor introduced a startup-breaking cycle `database/models.py` → `internal.bot.models` → `ensured_message` → `internal.database` that flake8/isort/pyright couldn't detect, since none execute imports). Implemented as:
   ```makefile
   @echo "Checking for circular imports..."
   $(PYTHON) -c "import main" || (echo "FAIL: circular import detected (or main.py cannot be imported)" && exit 1)
   ```
   `main.py` has an `if __name__ == "____main__":` guard so `import main` exercises only the import graph, not the bot runtime. On failure, Python's traceback (which pinpoints the cycle) prints first, then the friendly FAIL message.
4. `pyright` — `typeCheckingMode=basic`, excludes `ext/`, scopes to `.py`/`.ts`/`.js`.

ALL FOUR are Python-only. There is **NO markdown linter** wired anywhere in the Makefile or CI. The `check` target adds `black --check` — also Python-only.

**Convention for Makefile edits:** use the `$(PYTHON)` variable (= `./venv/bin/python`) for internal consistency within the Makefile, even though AGENTS.md's hard rule says to invoke `./venv/bin/python3` at the shell. The Makefile already defines and uses `$(PYTHON)` for all Python invocations; matching that is preferred over the literal `./venv/bin/python3`. Makefiles REQUIRE tabs (not spaces) for recipe indentation.

**Practical implication:** doc-only changes (`.md` files) are not touched by `make lint`. But note: AGENTS.md IS edited by Task 2 above, and `make lint` will still run clean on it (it's ignored).

title: GOTCHA: _runMemoryEmbeddingRegen is NOT exception-safe — resolveModel/toModel raises ValueError (caught by _dtCronJob caller)
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py`, the method `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` (around line 790) has a non-obvious exception contract.

**The chain:** The method calls `self.llmService.resolveModel(ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL, ...)` (around line 871-873) which is **unguarded** (not wrapped in try/except inside the method). `resolveModel` (service.py ~1079) calls `chatSettings[modelKey].toModel()`, and `ChatSettingsValue.toModel()` (chat_settings.py:589) raises `ValueError(f"Model {self.value} not found")` when the configured `EMBEDDING_MODEL` is empty or not registered in the model manager. This `ValueError` propagates out of `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen`.

**Why production is safe:** The caller — the `_dtCronJob` wrapper (around line 1028-1035) — wraps the `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen()` call in `try/except Exception`, so the exception is caught and the refinement pass on the same tick is unaffected.

**The gotcha:** Despite the overall cron design being robust (most failure paths log-and-return), this ONE path (model resolution, "step 4") is unguarded and CAN raise. Previously the method's docstring falsely claimed "Never raises — every failure path logs and returns" (fixed on 2026-07-09 to accurately document the ValueError + caller handling). Also note there is a STALE inline caller comment at ~line 1026 that STILL says "The method never raises, but the guard below ensures..." — this was left unfixed (the fix was scoped to the method's docstring only) and is known drift.

**Testing implication:** When writing tests that exercise `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen`, ensure the `EMBEDDING_MODEL` is registered in the mock model manager, or the method will raise ValueError.

title: dataSource convention: reads only for chat-scoped repos, writes route by chatId
content:
Convention for adding the `dataSource` parameter to repository methods in `internal/database/repositories/*.py`. Discovered 2026-07-09 while mapping the pattern for `UserMemoriesRepository`.

## Core rule: read/write asymmetry for chat-scoped repos

Chat-scoped repositories (tables with `chat_id`, e.g. `chat_messages`, `user_data`, and by extension `user_memories`) follow a deliberate convention:

- **READ methods** get `*, dataSource: Optional[str] = None` added, and call `getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`. This allows reads to cross into archive/explicit sources.
- **WRITE methods** do NOT take `dataSource`. They route purely by `chatId` via `getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=False)`. Writes must land where the chat is mapped (`chatMapping`). 

The canonical docstring note on write methods (verbatim, from `user_data.py:96,177,217` and `chat_messages.py:104`):
> "Writes are routed based on chatId mapping. Cannot write to readonly sources."

**Evidence:** `chat_messages.py` — `saveChatMessage`, `updateChatMessageCategory`, `updateChatMessageMetadata` (writes) have no `dataSource`; all 6 read methods have it. `user_data.py` — `addUserData`, `deleteUserData`, `clearUserData` (writes) have no `dataSource`; `getUserData` (read) has it.

## Exception: non-chat-scoped repos DO take dataSource on writes

Repositories whose tables have no `chat_id` concept (`cache.py`, `webhook_updates.py`, `common.py`, `delayed_tasks.py`) use `dataSource` directly on BOTH reads and writes, with NO `chatId`: `getProvider(dataSource=dataSource, readonly=False)`. There's no chat to route by, so the named source is the only routing key.

## Three getProvider call shapes (internal/database/manager.py:103-109)

```python
async def getProvider(self, *, chatId: Optional[int] = None,
                      dataSource: Optional[str] = None, readonly: bool = False)
```

- **(A) chatId only** — chat-scoped reads/writes without dataSource: `getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=True/False)`
- **(B) chatId + dataSource** — chat-scoped reads with explicit source: `getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`. dataSource takes priority over chatId mapping (manager.py:130).
- **(C) dataSource only** — non-chat-scoped repos: `getProvider(dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True/False)`, no chatId at all.

## Cross-provider aggregation sub-pattern (chat_users.py, chat_settings.py)

For methods that must union results across ALL databases (e.g. `getUserChats`, `getAllGroupChats`, `listChatsBySetting`), when `dataSource=None` the method loops over every provider:
```python
sourcesList = [dataSource] if dataSource else list(self.manager._providers.keys())
for sourceName in sourcesList:
    sqlProvider = await self.manager.getProvider(dataSource=sourceName, readonly=True)
    ...
```
NOTE (bug, see memory d784610f): `_providers.keys()` only covers lazily-initialized providers, not all configured sources. Used for aggregation queries, not single-chat lookups.

## dataSource routing priority in getProvider (3-tier)

1. Explicit `dataSource` param (highest)
2. `chatMapping[chatId]` lookup
3. `default` source (fallback)

title: dataSource type is Optional[str] deliberately (no StrEnum) — operator-configured provider keys
content:
Decision/convention about the `dataSource` parameter type in the Gromozeka multi-source DB architecture. Discovered 2026-07-09.

## The type: `Optional[str]`, uniformly

Everywhere — `DatabaseManager.getProvider()` (`internal/database/manager.py:107`), every repository method signature, every docstring — `dataSource` is typed `Optional[str]`, default `None`.

**There is deliberately NO enum** (no `StrEnum`, no `Literal[...]`). This is notable because the project's documented convention otherwise mandates `StrEnum` over `Literal[...]` for string-valued params. The `dataSource` value is a free-form string key.

## Why: values are operator-chosen config keys, not a fixed set

`dataSource` values are arbitrary strings matching keys under `[database.providers]` in TOML config. Examples seen in the wild: `"primary"`, `"archive"`, `"default"`, `"source1"`, `"source2"`, `"readonly_source"`, `"llm-stats-data-source"`, `"ds"`, `"other_bot"`. These are defined by operators in config, so a fixed enum would be wrong.

## Validation behavior

`getProvider` does NOT raise on an unknown source name. It logs a warning and silently falls back to the default provider (manager.py:131-135). `None` means "no explicit override → fall through to chatId mapping → default".

## How callers resolve dataSource (orchestration layer only)

`dataSource` is determined at the orchestration/config layer, NEVER inside a repo and NEVER from a `getChatSettings()` lookup. Examples:
- **Resender jobs** (`internal/bot/common/handlers/resender.py:119`): `dataSource` is a field on `ResenderJob`, set when the job is configured, threaded into every read.
- **LLM stats** (`main.py:84-87`): `statsConfig.get("llm-stats-data-source", self.database.manager.default)`.
- **Max webhook receiver** (`internal/max_webhook_receiver/app.py`): from receiver process config.

So when adding `dataSource` support to a repo method, you only need to accept and forward the param — the caller is responsible for sourcing the value.

title: MEMORIES_BLOCK_SOFT_CHAR_CAP defined but never used in code — suspected dead constant

title: Memory/backfill constants duplicated across DB and bot layers — name collisions
content:
Several tuning constants are duplicated or mirrored across the DB repository layer and the bot handler layer. These are maintenance hazards and name-collision gotchas for any constants-extraction or refactor of the memory/backfill code paths.

1. `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20` exists in BOTH:
   - `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:71` (repo default for `searchMemories`)
   - `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` (~line 89, bot default for the `search_memories` LLM tool)
   Same name, same value, DIFFERENT intent/layer. When extracting/centralizing, keep them in their respective layers and do NOT alias one to the other, or rename to disambiguate (e.g. `USER_MEMORIES_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`).

2. `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 50` is duplicated in 3 places with the same value and near-identical semantics:
   - `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:77` (DB repo)
   - `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:69` (bot, chat-history backfill)
   - `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` as `MEMORY_BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE` (bot, memory-embedding regen, prefixed)
   The docstrings explicitly call out the mirroring. Strongest case for a shared source of truth, but it straddles both layers.

3. `BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS = 0.1` (chat_search.py) and `MEMORY_BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS = 0.1` (user_data.py) mirror each other (same value 0.1), documented as intentional mirroring.

Context: `internal/database/constants.py` does NOT exist yet. DB-layer constants currently live scattered (e.g. `DEFAULT_THREAD_ID` in `internal/database/utils.py`, the user_memories constants inline in the repo). Bot-layer constants live inline in each handler, with cross-module ones re-exported via `internal/bot/models/__init__.py`. Any centralization plan must handle these collisions deliberately rather than merging by name.

title: dataSource read/write asymmetry convention for chat-scoped repositories
content:
Established pattern for adding `dataSource` multi-source DB support to chat-scoped repositories. Currently followed by `chat_messages.py` (reference), `user_data.py`, and `user_memories.py`.

## Read methods: add `dataSource`, pass to getProvider

- Signature: `dataSource: Optional[str] = None` as keyword-only param (last kwarg, after `*` or existing kwargs).
- `getProvider` call: `await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`
- Docstring: add `dataSource` to `Args:` section describing it as an optional provider key override.

## Write methods: NO `dataSource`, add Note to docstring

- Write methods do NOT accept `dataSource`. They call `await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=False)`.
- Docstring gets a `Note:` section: `"Writes are routed based on chatId mapping. Cannot write to readonly sources."`
- This matches the fact that write routing is determined by chatId-to-provider mapping, not by caller choice — you cannot write to an arbitrary source.

## Exception: private helpers receiving sqlProvider as a param

Some private helpers (e.g. `_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`) receive `sqlProvider` as a parameter rather than calling `getProvider` themselves. These do NOT get `dataSource` — the calling write method already obtained the provider. Verify the chain when adding `dataSource` to a public method that delegates to such helpers.

## Forwarding through intermediate methods

When a public read method delegates to private helpers that also call `getProvider` (e.g. `searchMemories` → `_filterOnlySearchMemories` + `_semanticSearchMemories`), `dataSource` must be forwarded through ALL methods in the call chain, not just the top-level one.

## When adding to a new repo

Use `chat_messages.py` as the reference implementation. The `dataSource` param is always keyword-only, always `Optional[str] = None`, always last in the kwargs list.

title: internal/database/constants.py exists — DB-layer constants, no bot-layer imports
content:
`internal/database/constants.py` was created (2026-07-09) to centralize DB-layer tuning constants, superseding inline definitions in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py`.

## Contents (5 constants)

- `PERMANENT_INJECTION_CAP: int = 10` — max permanent memories per (chatId, userId) per turn
- `EPHEMERAL_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT: int = 5` — default cap on ephemeral (non-permanent) memories per turn

- `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE: int = 50` — default per-tick batch size for embedding-regen cron

If a constant is needed by both layers, each layer defines its own copy (see memory 88d6b37d about cross-layer duplication hazards).

- Bot-layer constants (e.g. `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT` in `user_data.py`) were NOT consolidated here — they remain in their respective handler modules per the layering rule.

## This supersedes memory 88d6b37d's claim that "internal/database/constants.py does NOT exist yet"

The DB-layer side of the constants duplication is now resolved. The cross-layer duplication (bot-layer copies of `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`, etc.) still exists and remains a maintenance hazard per memory 88d6b37d.

title: internal/bot/constants.py — canonical home for bot-layer constants (handlers + models)
content:
As of 2026-07-09, `internal/bot/constants.py` is the single canonical home for module-level `UPPER_CASE` constants that were previously defined inline in bot handler files and bot model files. This mirrors the DB-layer `internal/database/constants.py`.

- From `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` (13): memory refinement thresholds (`MEMORY_COUNT_THRESHOLD`, `MEMORY_TIME_THRESHOLD_SECONDS`, `MEMORY_MIN_MESSAGES_TO_REFINE`, `MEMORY_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_RUN`, `MEMORY_MAX_REFINES_PER_TICK`), dedup thresholds (`MEMORY_DEDUP_DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD`, `MEMORY_DEDUP_SIMILAR_THRESHOLD`), search limits (`MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `MEMORY_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT`), embedding regen (`MEMORY_BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`, `MEMORY_BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS`), knowledge-config wizard (`KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE`, `KNOWLEDGE_CONFIG_TAG_FILTER_FETCH_LIMIT`).
- From `chat_search.py` (5): `SEARCH_DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS`, `SEARCH_DEFAULT_DAYS`, `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`, `SEARCH_TOOL_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`, `BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS`.
- From `sandbox.py` (2): `MAX_SANDBOX_READ_FILE_BYTES` (64KB), `MAX_SANDBOX_SEND_BYTES` (20MB).
- From `models/chat_settings.py` (2): `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_LATEST` ("latest"), `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_RELEVANT` ("relevant").

Constants are organized with section-comment headers + trailing per-constant docstrings (matching the file's existing style).

## Backwards-compat re-export
`internal/bot/models/__init__.py` re-exports `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_LATEST`/`MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODE_RELEVANT` from `internal.bot.constants` so legacy `from internal.bot.models import ...` keeps working. The canonical consumer path is now direct: `from internal.bot.constants import ...` (e.g. `message_preprocessor.py` imports directly). Single definition, two valid import paths.

## Intentional cross-layer duplication (NOT a hazard to merge)
Some constant NAMES exist in BOTH `internal/bot/constants.py` AND `internal/database/constants.py` — e.g. `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT` (20) and `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE` (50). This duplication is INTENTIONAL and correct: the DB layer sits below the bot layer and must NOT import `internal.bot.*` (circular-import risk). Each layer keeps its own copy. Do NOT try to merge them into one shared source of truth. (This supersedes the prior framing of the duplication as a "maintenance hazard".)

## Intentionally NOT moved (file-local)
- `internal/bot/models/text_formatter.py` — `FORMATER_ENCODING` etc. (genuinely file-local)
- `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py` — `MAX_MEDIA_AWAIT_SECS`, `MEDIA_AWAIT_DELAY`, `WORD_BREAKERS` (genuinely file-local)
- `internal/database/constants.py` — separate layer, left untouched.

## Convention for new bot constants
New module-level UPPER_CASE constants for bot handlers/models should be added to `internal/bot/constants.py` (with a section header + docstring), then imported by the consuming file. Do NOT reintroduce inline definitions in handler/model files.

title: Mirror constants drift risk: MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT & BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE duplicated across bot/db layers with no parity guard
content:
GOTCHA discovered in code review (2026-07-09, branch `user-memory-v2`, reviewer verdict: mergeable with this 🔵 finding).

After the constants-centralization refactor (constants extracted from handler/model files into `internal/bot/constants.py` and `internal/database/constants.py`), two constants are deliberately **mirrored** (defined identically) in BOTH layer-specific constants files:

- `MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20` — `internal/bot/constants.py:184` AND `internal/database/constants.py:15`
- `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 50` — `internal/bot/constants.py:243` AND `internal/database/constants.py:22`

The duplication is **intentional** (layer separation: bot-layer shouldn't depend on db-layer constants and vice versa), and the docstrings cross-reference each other ("Mirrors …"). But parity is enforced **only by human discipline** — there is NO test asserting the two layer-specific copies stay equal.

## Why it matters
The bot-layer value and the db-layer value are meant to track, but if someone changes one without the other, the drift is silent. The existing test at `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data_memory_regen.py:647` asserts `MEMORY_BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE == 50` (absolute value) but never asserts it equals its db-layer sibling. So a divergence would not be caught.

## Suggested fix (lighter touch)
Add a parity test, e.g.:
```python
assert bot_constants.BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE == db_constants.BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE
assert bot_constants.MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT == db_constants.MEMORY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT
```
The alternative — consolidating to a single definition by letting `internal.bot` import `internal.database` — is heavier and may be undesirable for layering. The deliberate mirror pattern is defensible; a guard test closes the drift gap without coupling layers.

## Related
This mirrors the general "stale-after-move" hazard (memory 9ee8199d, test-file-move docstrings) applied to the constants-centralization refactor: two cross-referencing copies of a value are a maintenance liability unless mechanically pinned.

title: Wizard free-text input pattern restored + manual memory creation (memory_config)
content:
As of 2026-07-09, the `/memory_config` (formerly `/knowledge_config`) wizard gained a manual memory-creation feature. This **RESTORED the free-text input path** that Phase 5a had deliberately removed from `newMessageHandler` (memory `f698fd93` documented that removal). The `UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig` enum member — which Phase 5a kept "for reuse in Phase 5b" — is now actively used again.

## Reusable pattern: adding a free-text input step to the wizard
To add a free-text input step (e.g. "type the memory content"):

1. **Handler sets user state** via `self.cache.setUserState(userId=user.id, stateKey=UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig, value={"data": {...payload with the follow-up action...}, "messageId": messageId, "messageChatId": messageChatId})`. The `UserActiveConfigurationDict` requires all three keys: `data`, `messageId`, `messageChatId`.
2. **`newMessageHandler` checks state** AFTER the memory-refinement accounting block, BEFORE `return HandlerResultStatus.NEXT`: `getUserState(userId, stateKey=UserActiveActionEnum.UserDataConfig)`. If present, it injects the message text as `ButtonDataKey.Value` and routes through `_handleUserDataConfiguration` (the dispatcher), returning `HandlerResultStatus.FINAL`.
3. **Dispatcher clears state at the TOP** (`self.cache.clearUserState(...)`) BEFORE dispatching to the action handler — so the handler that SETS state runs AFTER the clear (correct ordering), and the consuming handler runs AFTER the state is cleared (no double-consume).

This is safe for all messages: `getUserState` returns `None` for users without active wizard state, so non-wizard messages fall through to `NEXT` unchanged.

## Manual memory creation specifics
New enum members in `ButtonUserDataConfigAction`: `AddMemory = "am"`, `SetMemoryContent = "sm"`.
- The "➕ Добавить память" button appears in `_renderMemoryList` ONLY when a specific type is selected (`typeFilterRaw != "all"`), placed after memory buttons, before nav/filter buttons.
- Created memories: `permanent=False` (ephemeral), `source=UserMemorySource.USER`, `embedding=None` / `embeddingModel=None` (the regen cron embeds them later), `tags=[]`, `threadId=DEFAULT_THREAD_ID` (0).
- Content validation: empty/whitespace-only content renders an error, no memory created.

## Key gotchas confirmed
- The DB converter returns real `bool` for `permanent` (not int 0/1), so `assert mem["permanent"] is False` works.
- `StrEnum` values compare with `==` to their string values but NOT `is`.
- `addMemory` signature: positional `chatId, userId, memoryId`, then keyword-only `type, content, tags, permanent, source, embedding, embeddingModel` (optional `threadId`).
- Tests: the restored `newMessageHandler` path calls `getChatSettings` (for accounting); stub it with `_stubGetChatSettings(handler, memoryRefinementEnabled=False)` in tests.

title: Incomplete rename: memory_config helpMessage/launch strings still say "знаниями" (knowledge)
content:

\"знаниями\" = \"knowledge\". The wizard's own UI (added in the same change) uses \"память\" (memory) throughout (\"➕ Добавить память\", \"Память добавлена\", \"Память удалена\"). So the `/help` entry for `/memory_config` now contradicts both the command name and the wizard it launches.
